    33→  return (phase, meta) => {
    34→    const payload: Record<string, unknown> = {
    35→      shotId: shortTimelineId(meta.shotId),
    36→      requestId: meta.requestId,
    37→      operation: meta.operation,
    38→      waitMs: meta.waitMs,
    39→      queueDepth: meta.queueDepth,
    40→      blockedByOperation: meta.blockedByOperation ?? null,
    41→      blockedByDurationMs: meta.blockedByDurationMs ?? null,
    42→    };
    43→
    44→    if (phase !== 'start') {
    45→      payload.durationMs = meta.durationMs;
    46→    }
    47→
    48→    log(`${options.logPrefix} write queue ${phase}`, payload);
    49→  };
    50→}
    51→
    52→const DEFAULT_TIMELINE_WRITE_TIMEOUT_MS = 15_000;
    53→const TIMELINE_WRITE_TIMEOUT_CODE = 'TIMELINE_WRITE_TIMEOUT';
    54→
    55→interface TimelineWriteTimeoutOptions {
    56→  timeoutMs?: number;
    57→  onTimeout?: (meta: { operation: string; timeoutMs: number; pendingMs: number }) => void;
    58→}
    59→
    60→class TimelineWriteTimeoutError extends Error {
    61→  readonly code = TIMELINE_WRITE_TIMEOUT_CODE;
    62→
    63→  constructor(operation: string, timeoutMs: number, cause?: unknown) {
    64→    super(`Timeline write "${operation}" timed out after ${timeoutMs}ms`);
    65→    this.name = 'TimelineWriteTimeoutError';
    66→    if (cause !== undefined) {
    67→      (this as { cause?: unknown }).cause = cause;
    68→    }
    69→  }
    70→}
    71→
    72→export function isTimelineWriteTimeoutError(error: unknown): error is TimelineWriteTimeoutError {
    73→  return (
    74→    error instanceof TimelineWriteTimeoutError
    75→    || (
    76→      typeof error === 'object'
    77→      && error !== null
    78→      && 'code' in error
    79→      && (error as { code?: unknown }).code === TIMELINE_WRITE_TIMEOUT_CODE
    80→    )
    81→  );
    82→}
    83→
    84→/**
    85→ * Guard a write request with an abortable timeout so stalled network calls
    86→ * cannot block the serialized per-shot queue forever.
    87→ */
    88→export async function runTimelineWriteWithTimeout<T>(
    89→  operation: string,
    90→  task: (signal: AbortSignal) => Promise<T>,
    91→  options?: TimelineWriteTimeoutOptions,
    92→): Promise<T> {
    93→  const timeoutMs = options?.timeoutMs ?? DEFAULT_TIMELINE_WRITE_TIMEOUT_MS;
    94→  const startedAt = Date.now();
    95→  const controller = new AbortController();
    96→  let timedOut = false;
    97→
    98→  const timeoutId = setTimeout(() => {
    99→    timedOut = true;
   100→    options?.onTimeout?.({
   101→      operation,
   102→      timeoutMs,
   103→      pendingMs: Date.now() - startedAt,
   104→    });
   105→    controller.abort();
   106→  }, timeoutMs);
   107→
   108→  try {
   109→    return await task(controller.signal);
   110→  } catch (error) {
   111→    if (timedOut || (controller.signal.aborted && isAbortError(error))) {
   112→      throw new TimelineWriteTimeoutError(operation, timeoutMs, error);
   113→    }
   114→    throw error;
   115→  } finally {
   116→    clearTimeout(timeoutId);
   117→  }
   118→}
   119→
   120→const shotWriteTail = new Map<string, Promise<void>>();
   121→const shotWriteDepth = new Map<string, number>();
   122→const shotWriteActive = new Map<string, { requestId: number; operation: string; startedAt: number }>();
   123→let writeRequestCounter = 0;
   124→const DEFAULT_SERIALIZED_TIMELINE_TASK_TIMEOUT_MS = 30_000;
   125→
   126→interface TimelineSerializedWriteOptions {
   127→  timeoutMs?: number;
   128→  onTimeout?: (meta: {
   129→    shotId: string;
   130→    operation: string;
   131→    timeoutMs: number;
   132→    pendingMs: number;
   133→    requestId: number;
   134→  }) => void;
   135→}
   136→
   137→function runSerializedTaskWithTimeout<T>(
   138→  operation: string,
   139→  task: () => Promise<T>,
   140→  timeoutMs: number,
   141→  onTimeout: () => void,
   142→): Promise<T> {
   143→  if (timeoutMs <= 0) {
   144→    return task();
   145→  }
   146→
   147→  return new Promise<T>((resolve, reject) => {
   148→    let settled = false;
   149→    const timeoutId = setTimeout(() => {
   150→      if (settled) {
   151→        return;
   152→      }
   153→      settled = true;
   154→      onTimeout();
   155→      reject(new TimelineWriteTimeoutError(operation, timeoutMs));
   156→    }, timeoutMs);
   157→
   158→    Promise.resolve()
   159→      .then(task)
   160→      .then(
   161→        (result) => {
   162→          if (settled) {
   163→            return;
   164→          }
   165→          settled = true;
   166→          clearTimeout(timeoutId);
   167→          resolve(result);
   168→        },
   169→        (error) => {
   170→          if (settled) {
   171→            return;
   172→          }
   173→          settled = true;
   174→          clearTimeout(timeoutId);
   175→          reject(error);
   176→        },
   177→      );
   178→  });
   179→}
   180→
   181→/**
   182→ * Returns true if any serialized timeline write is active or queued for the
   183→ * given shot. Both the timeline drag path and the batch editor path go through
   184→ * runSerializedTimelineWrite, so this covers all writes across both paths.
   185→ * Used by useTimelinePositions.syncFromDatabase to suppress stale syncs while
   186→ * the batch editor is writing (the batch editor does not set isLockedRef, so
   187→ * without this check a background refetch during the midpoint RPC would snap
   188→ * positions back to pre-edit values).
   189→ */
   190→export function isTimelineWriteActive(shotId: string): boolean {
   191→  return (shotWriteDepth.get(shotId) ?? 0) > 0;
   192→}
   193→
   194→/**
   195→ * Serialize timeline writes per shot to avoid overlapping updates from
   196→ * different UI flows (batch reorder, timeline drag, etc.).
   197→ */
   198→export async function runSerializedTimelineWrite<T>(
   199→  shotId: string,
   200→  operation: string,
   201→  task: () => Promise<T>,
   202→  onEvent?: TimelineWriteEventHandler,
   203→  options?: TimelineSerializedWriteOptions,
   204→): Promise<T> {
   205→  const requestId = ++writeRequestCounter;
   206→  const queuedAt = Date.now();
   207→  const previousTail = shotWriteTail.get(shotId) ?? Promise.resolve();
   208→  const nextDepth = (shotWriteDepth.get(shotId) ?? 0) + 1;
   209→  shotWriteDepth.set(shotId, nextDepth);
   210→  const blockedBy = shotWriteActive.get(shotId);
   211→  const blockedByDurationMs = blockedBy ? Math.max(0, queuedAt - blockedBy.startedAt) : null;
   212→
   213→  onEvent?.('queued', {
   214→    shotId,
   215→    operation,
   216→    waitMs: 0,
   217→    durationMs: 0,
   218→    queueDepth: Math.max(0, nextDepth - 1),
   219→    requestId,
   220→    blockedByOperation: blockedBy?.operation ?? null,
   221→    blockedByDurationMs,
   222→  });
   223→
   224→  let releaseTail!: () => void;
   225→  const currentTail = new Promise<void>((resolve) => {
   226→    releaseTail = resolve;
   227→  });
   228→
   229→  const chainedTail = previousTail.catch(() => undefined).then(() => currentTail);
   230→  shotWriteTail.set(shotId, chainedTail);
   231→
   232→  await previousTail.catch(() => undefined);
   233→
   234→  const startedAt = Date.now();
   235→  shotWriteActive.set(shotId, {
   236→    requestId,
   237→    operation,
   238→    startedAt,
   239→  });
   240→  onEvent?.('start', {
   241→    shotId,
   242→    operation,
   243→    waitMs: startedAt - queuedAt,
   244→    durationMs: 0,
   245→    queueDepth: Math.max(0, (shotWriteDepth.get(shotId) ?? 1) - 1),
   246→    requestId,
   247→    blockedByOperation: blockedBy?.operation ?? null,
   248→    blockedByDurationMs,
   249→  });
   250→
   251→  try {
   252→    const timeoutMs = options?.timeoutMs ?? DEFAULT_SERIALIZED_TIMELINE_TASK_TIMEOUT_MS;
   253→    return await runSerializedTaskWithTimeout(
   254→      operation,
   255→      task,
   256→      timeoutMs,
   257→      () => {
   258→        options?.onTimeout?.({
   259→          shotId,
   260→          operation,
   261→          timeoutMs,
   262→          pendingMs: Date.now() - startedAt,
   263→          requestId,
   264→        });
   265→      },
   266→    );
   267→  } finally {
   268→    releaseTail();
   269→
   270→    const remainingDepth = Math.max(0, (shotWriteDepth.get(shotId) ?? 1) - 1);
   271→    if (remainingDepth === 0) {
   272→      shotWriteDepth.delete(shotId);
   273→    } else {
   274→      shotWriteDepth.set(shotId, remainingDepth);
   275→    }
   276→
   277→    if (shotWriteTail.get(shotId) === chainedTail) {
   278→      shotWriteTail.delete(shotId);
   279→    }
   280→    if (shotWriteActive.get(shotId)?.requestId === requestId) {
   281→      shotWriteActive.delete(shotId);
   282→    }
   283→
   284→    onEvent?.('end', {
   285→      shotId,
   286→      operation,
   287→      waitMs: startedAt - queuedAt,
   288→      durationMs: Date.now() - startedAt,
   289→      queueDepth: Math.max(0, remainingDepth - 1),
   290→      requestId,
   291→      blockedByOperation: blockedBy?.operation ?? null,
   292→      blockedByDurationMs,
   293→    });
   294→  }
   295→}
   296→

## Your Dimensions

### package_organization
Description: Directory layout quality and navigability: whether placement matches ownership and change boundaries
Look for:
- Straggler roots: root-level files with low fan-in that share concern with other files should move under a focused package
- Import-affinity mismatch: file imports/references are mostly from one sibling domain but lives outside that domain
- Flat directory overload: >10 files with mixed concerns should be split into purpose-driven subfolders
- Ambiguous folder naming: directory names do not reflect contained responsibilities
Skip:
- Root-level files that ARE genuinely core (high fan-in, imported across multiple subdirectories)
- Framework-imposed directory layouts (src/, lib/, dist/)

### initialization_coupling
Description: Boot-order dependencies, import-time side effects, global singletons
Look for:
- Module-level code that depends on another module having been imported first
- Import-time side effects: DB connections, file I/O, network calls at module scope
- Global singletons where creation order matters across modules
- Environment variable reads at import time
- Circular init dependencies hidden behind conditional or lazy imports
Skip:
- Standard library initialization (logging.basicConfig)
- Framework bootstrap (app.configure, server.listen)

### design_coherence
Description: Are structural design decisions sound — functions focused, abstractions earned, patterns consistent?
Look for:
- Functions doing too many things — multiple distinct responsibilities in one body
- Parameter lists that should be config/context objects
- Deep nesting that could be flattened with early returns or extraction
- Repeated structural patterns that should be data-driven
Skip:
- Functions that are long but have a single coherent responsibility
- Nesting that is inherent to the problem

    46→
    47→## Tech Stack
    48→
    49→| Layer | Technology | Purpose |
    50→|-------|------------|---------|
    51→| **Frontend** | React + Vite + TypeScript | SPA framework & build tooling |
    52→| **Styling** | TailwindCSS + shadcn-ui | Utility CSS with container queries (`@container`) |
    53→| **Backend** | Supabase (Postgres + Edge Functions) | Database, auth, storage, serverless workers |
    54→
    55→**Dev server:** `http://localhost:2222` • **Package managers:** npm (default) or bun
    56→
    57→---
    58→
    59→## Directory Structure
    60→
    61→| Path | Purpose | Key Files |
    62→|------|---------|-----------|
    63→| `/src/app` | App bootstrap & routing | `main.tsx` → `App.tsx` → `routes.tsx` → `Layout.tsx` |
    64→| `/src/pages` | Top-level pages | `HomePage`, `ShotsPage`, `ArtPage`, `SharePage`, `NotFoundPage`, payment pages |
    65→| `/src/tools` | Feature modules | Each tool: `pages/`, `components/`, `hooks/`, `settings.ts` |
    66→| `/src/shared` | Shared code | `components/ui/` (shadcn), `hooks/`, `contexts/`, `lib/` |
    67→| `/supabase/functions` | Edge Functions | Task processing, payments, AI integration |
    68→| `/supabase/migrations` | DB migrations | Schema changes (use `db push --linked`) |
    69→| Root | Build configs | `vite.config.ts`, `tailwind.config.ts`, `railway.toml` |
    70→
    71→---
    72→
    73→## Core Concepts
    74→
    75→### Tools
    76→Tools live in `/src/tools/{tool-name}/` following a consistent structure. See [adding_new_tool.md](docs/structure_detail/adding_new_tool.md).
    77→
    78→**Active tools:** Image Generation, Video Travel, Animate Characters, Edit Images, Edit Video, Join Clips, Training Data Helper
    79→
    80→### Shots & Generations
    81→- **Generations** = gallery items (images/videos produced by AI tasks)
    82→- **Shots** = containers that organize generations into a timeline
    83→- **`shot_generations`** = join table with position + metadata (pair prompts, timeline frame)
    84→- Data access: `useShotImages(shotId)` → see [data_fetching.md](docs/structure_detail/data_fetching.md)
    85→
    86→### Settings Resolution
    87→Priority: **shot → project → user → defaults**. See [settings_system.md](docs/structure_detail/settings_system.md).
    88→
    89→### Task System
    90→Async queue for AI workloads: client creates task → DB trigger → worker polls → Edge Function completes.
    91→See [task_worker_lifecycle.md](docs/structure_detail/task_worker_lifecycle.md).
    92→
    93→### Realtime
    94→Smart polling + Supabase realtime subscriptions. Connected = no polling; disconnected = 15s fallback.
    95→See [realtime_system.md](docs/structure_detail/realtime_system.md).
    96→
    97→---
    98→
    99→## Key Utilities
   100→
   101→| System | Location | Purpose |
   102→|--------|----------|---------|
   103→| **queryKeys** | `lib/queryKeys.ts` | Central registry for all React Query cache keys |
   104→| **errors** | `lib/errors.ts` | Typed error classes (`NetworkError`, `AuthError`, `ValidationError`, etc.) |
   105→| **errorHandler** | `lib/errorHandler.ts` | Centralized `handleError()` with logging + toast |
   106→| **AppErrorBoundary** | `components/AppErrorBoundary.tsx` | App-level crash recovery UI |
   107→| **ModalContainer** | `components/ModalContainer.tsx` | Unified responsive modal with header/footer/scroll |
   108→| **ConfirmDialog** | `components/ConfirmDialog.tsx` | Promise-based confirmation dialogs with presets |
   109→| **settingsResolution** | `lib/settingsResolution.ts` | Resolve settings across scopes |
   110→| **settingsWriteQueue** | `lib/settingsWriteQueue.ts` | Global queue for settings writes (prevents network flooding) |
   111→| **debugConfig** | `lib/debugConfig.ts` | Runtime debug logging (`window.debugConfig`) |
   112→| **taskConfig** | `lib/taskConfig.ts` | Task visibility & display names |
   113→| **performanceUtils** | `lib/performanceUtils.ts` | Frame budget monitoring |
   114→
   115→Instrumentation lives in `src/integrations/supabase/instrumentation/` — see its [README](src/integrations/supabase/instrumentation/README.md).
   116→
   117→---
   118→

   120→

   122→

1→import { TaskValidationError } from './types';
     2→
     3→/**
     4→ * Validates that required fields are present and non-empty.
     5→ */
     6→export function validateRequiredFields(params: object, requiredFields: readonly string[]): void {
     7→  const values = params as Record<string, unknown>;
     8→  for (const field of requiredFields) {
     9→    const value = values[field];
    10→
    11→    if (value === undefined || value === null) {
    12→      throw new TaskValidationError(`${field} is required`, field);
    13→    }
    14→
    15→    // Check for empty arrays
    16→    if (Array.isArray(value) && value.length === 0) {
    17→      throw new TaskValidationError(`${field} cannot be empty`, field);
    18→    }
    19→
    20→    // Check for empty strings
    21→    if (typeof value === 'string' && value.trim() === '') {
    22→      throw new TaskValidationError(`${field} cannot be empty`, field);
    23→    }
    24→  }
    25→}
    26→
    27→/**
    28→ * Safely parses JSON string with fallback.
    29→ */
    30→export function safeParseJson<T>(jsonStr: string | undefined, fallback: T): T {
    31→  if (!jsonStr) return fallback;
    32→
    33→  try {
    34→    return JSON.parse(jsonStr) as T;
    35→  } catch {
    36→    return fallback;
    37→  }
    38→}
    39→

1→import { TaskValidationError } from './types';
     2→import type { PathLoraConfig } from '@/shared/types/lora';
     3→
     4→interface NumericRangeOptions {
     5→  field: string;
     6→  label: string;
     7→  min: number;
     8→  max: number;
     9→}
    10→
    11→interface LoraValidationOptions<
    12→  T extends Record<string, unknown>,
    13→  TPathField extends keyof T,
    14→  TStrengthField extends keyof T,
    15→> {
    16→  pathField: TPathField;
    17→  strengthField: TStrengthField;
    18→  strengthLabel: string;
    19→  min: number;
    20→  max: number;
    21→}
    22→
    23→interface ResolveSeed32BitOptions {
    24→  seed?: number;
    25→  randomize?: boolean;
    26→  fallbackSeed?: number;
    27→  field?: string;
    28→}
    29→
    30→export const MAX_SEED_32_BIT = 0x7fffffff;
    31→
    32→export function validateNonEmptyString(
    33→  value: string,
    34→  field: string,
    35→  label: string,
    36→): void {
    37→  if (value.trim() === '') {
    38→    throw new TaskValidationError(`${label} cannot be empty`, field);
    39→  }
    40→}
    41→
    42→export function validateUrlString(
    43→  value: string,
    44→  field: string,
    45→  label: string,
    46→): void {
    47→  try {
    48→    new URL(value);
    49→  } catch {
    50→    throw new TaskValidationError(`${label} must be a valid URL`, field);
    51→  }
    52→}
    53→
    54→export function validateNumericRange(
    55→  value: number | undefined,
    56→  { field, label, min, max }: NumericRangeOptions,
    57→): void {
    58→  if (value === undefined) {
    59→    return;
    60→  }
    61→  if (value < min || value > max) {
    62→    throw new TaskValidationError(`${label} must be between ${min} and ${max}`, field);
    63→  }
    64→}
    65→
    66→export function validateSeed32Bit(seed: number | undefined, field = 'seed'): void {
    67→  validateNumericRange(seed, {
    68→    field,
    69→    label: 'Seed',
    70→    min: 0,
    71→    max: MAX_SEED_32_BIT,
    72→  });
    73→}
    74→
    75→export function generateSeed32Bit(): number {
    76→  return Math.floor(Math.random() * MAX_SEED_32_BIT);
    77→}
    78→
    79→export function resolveSeed32Bit({
    80→  seed,
    81→  randomize = false,
    82→  fallbackSeed,
    83→  field = 'seed',
    84→}: ResolveSeed32BitOptions): number {
    85→  if (randomize) {
    86→    return generateSeed32Bit();
    87→  }
    88→
    89→  const resolvedSeed = seed ?? fallbackSeed;
    90→  if (resolvedSeed !== undefined) {
    91→    validateSeed32Bit(resolvedSeed, field);
    92→    return resolvedSeed;
    93→  }
    94→
    95→  return generateSeed32Bit();
    96→}
    97→
    98→export function validateLoraConfigs<
    99→  T extends Record<string, unknown>,
   100→  TPathField extends keyof T,
   101→  TStrengthField extends keyof T,
   102→>(
   103→  loras: T[] | undefined,
   104→  options: LoraValidationOptions<T, TPathField, TStrengthField>,
   105→): void {
   106→  if (!loras?.length) {
   107→    return;
   108→  }
   109→
   110→  const {
   111→    pathField,
   112→    strengthField,
   113→    strengthLabel,
   114→    min,
   115→    max,
   116→  } = options;
   117→
   118→  loras.forEach((lora, index) => {
   119→    const pathValue = lora[pathField];
   120→    if (typeof pathValue !== 'string' || pathValue.trim() === '') {
   121→      throw new TaskValidationError(`LoRA ${index + 1}: path is required`, `loras[${index}].${String(pathField)}`);
   122→    }
   123→
   124→    const strengthValue = lora[strengthField];
   125→    if (typeof strengthValue !== 'number') {
   126→      throw new TaskValidationError(`LoRA ${index + 1}: ${strengthLabel} is required`, `loras[${index}].${String(strengthField)}`);
   127→    }
   128→    if (strengthValue < min || strengthValue > max) {
   129→      throw new TaskValidationError(
   130→        `LoRA ${index + 1}: ${strengthLabel} must be between ${min} and ${max}`,
   131→        `loras[${index}].${String(strengthField)}`,
   132→      );
   133→    }
   134→  });
   135→}
   136→
   137→export function mapPathLorasToStrengthRecord(
   138→  loras: PathLoraConfig[] | undefined,
   139→): Record<string, number> {
   140→  if (!loras?.length) {
   141→    return {};
   142→  }
   143→
   144→  return loras.reduce<Record<string, number>>((acc, lora) => {
   145→    if (lora.path) {
   146→      acc[lora.path] = lora.strength;
   147→    }
   148→    return acc;
   149→  }, {});
   150→}

    51→function filterReferenceSettingsByMode(

   225→/**
   226→ * Options for calculateTaskResolution
   227→ */
   228→interface CalculateTaskResolutionOptions {
   229→  /** Project ID for resolution lookup */
   230→  projectId: string;
   231→  /** Optional explicit resolution override (bypasses all calculations) */
   232→  customResolution?: string;
   233→  /** Model name (determines if scaling is applied) */
   234→  modelName?: string;
   235→  /** User-configurable resolution scale multiplier (1.0-2.5x). Defaults to 1.5 for image models. */
   236→  resolution_scale?: number;
   237→  /** Resolution mode: 'project' uses project dimensions, 'custom' uses custom_aspect_ratio */
   238→  resolution_mode?: 'project' | 'custom';
   239→  /** Custom aspect ratio when resolution_mode is 'custom' (e.g., "16:9") */
   240→  custom_aspect_ratio?: string;
   241→}
   242→
   243→/**
   244→ * Calculates the final resolution for image generation tasks.
   245→ * Applies user-configurable scaling for supported image generation models.
   246→ * (internal use only - not exported)
   247→ * @param options - Resolution calculation options
   248→ * @returns Promise resolving to the final resolution string
   249→ */
   250→async function calculateTaskResolution(
   251→  options: CalculateTaskResolutionOptions
   252→): Promise<string> {
   253→  const { projectId, resolution_scale, resolution_mode, custom_aspect_ratio } = options;
   254→
   255→  // 1. If explicit custom resolution is provided, use it as-is (assumes it's already final)
   256→  if (options.customResolution?.trim()) {
   257→    return options.customResolution.trim();
   258→  }
   259→
   260→  // 2. Determine base resolution
   261→  let baseResolution: string;
   262→
   263→  if (resolution_mode === 'custom' && custom_aspect_ratio) {
   264→    // Use custom aspect ratio
   265→    baseResolution = ASPECT_RATIO_TO_RESOLUTION[custom_aspect_ratio] ?? '902x508';
   266→  } else {
   267→    // Use project resolution
   268→    const { resolution } = await resolveProjectResolution(projectId);
   269→    baseResolution = resolution;
   270→  }
   271→
   272→  // 3. Apply scaling for image generation models
   273→  const isImageGenerationModel = options.modelName === 'qwen-image' || options.modelName === 'qwen-image-2512' || options.modelName === 'z-image';
   274→  if (isImageGenerationModel) {
   275→    const scale = resolution_scale ?? 1.5; // Default to 1.5 if not specified
   276→    const [width, height] = baseResolution.split('x').map(Number);
   277→    const scaledWidth = Math.round(width * scale);
   278→    const scaledHeight = Math.round(height * scale);
   279→    const scaledResolution = `${scaledWidth}x${scaledHeight}`;
   280→    return scaledResolution;
   281→  }
   282→
   283→  return baseResolution;
   284→}

   382→/**
   383→ * Creates a single image generation task using the unified approach
   384→ * This replaces the direct call to the single-image-generate edge function
   385→ * (internal use only - used by createBatchImageGenerationTasks)
   386→ *
   387→ * @param params - Image generation task parameters
   388→ * @returns Promise resolving to the created task
   389→ */
   390→async function createImageGenerationTask(params: ImageGenerationTaskParams): Promise<TaskCreationResult> {
   391→  return runTaskCreationPipeline({
   392→    params,
   393→    context: 'ImageGeneration',
   394→    validate: validateImageGenerationParams,
   395→    buildTaskRequest: async (requestParams) => {
   396→      // 1. Calculate final resolution (handles Qwen scaling automatically)
   397→      const finalResolution = await calculateTaskResolution({
   398→        projectId: requestParams.project_id,
   399→        customResolution: requestParams.resolution,
   400→        modelName: requestParams.model_name,
   401→      });
   402→
   403→      // 2. Determine task type based on model and whether there's a style reference
   404→      const taskType = (() => {
   405→        const modelName = requestParams.model_name;
   406→        const hasStyleRef = !!requestParams.style_reference_image;
   407→
   408→        switch (modelName) {
   409→          case 'qwen-image':
   410→            // Use qwen_image_style for by-reference mode, qwen_image for just-text
   411→            return hasStyleRef ? 'qwen_image_style' : 'qwen_image';
   412→          case 'qwen-image-2512':
   413→            return 'qwen_image_2512';
   414→          case 'z-image':
   415→            return 'z_image_turbo';
   416→          default:
   417→            // Fallback to wan_2_2_t2i for unknown models
   418→            return 'wan_2_2_t2i';
   419→        }
   420→      })();
   421→      const supportsReferenceParamsModel =
   422→        requestParams.model_name?.startsWith('qwen-image') || requestParams.model_name === 'z-image';
   423→
   424→      // 3. Generate task ID for orchestration payload (stored in params, not as DB ID)
   425→      const taskId = generateTaskId(taskType);
   426→
   427→      // 4. Build intermediate params before assembling the final object
   428→      const lorasParam = buildLorasParam(
   429→        requestParams.loras,
   430→        supportsReferenceParamsModel && requestParams.in_this_scene && requestParams.in_this_scene_strength
   431→          ? { url: IN_SCENE_LORA_URL, strength: requestParams.in_this_scene_strength }
   432→          : undefined,
   433→      );
   434→      const referenceParams = supportsReferenceParamsModel
   435→        ? buildReferenceParams(requestParams.style_reference_image, requestParams.reference_mode, {
   436→            subjectReferenceImage: requestParams.subject_reference_image,
   437→            styleReferenceStrength: requestParams.style_reference_strength ?? 1.0,
   438→            subjectStrength: requestParams.subject_strength ?? 0.0,
   439→            subjectDescription: requestParams.subject_description,
   440→            inThisScene: requestParams.in_this_scene,
   441→            inThisSceneStrength: requestParams.in_this_scene_strength,
   442→          })
   443→        : {};
   444→      const hiresOverride = buildHiresOverride(
   445→        requestParams.hires_scale,
   446→        requestParams.hires_denoise,
   447→        requestParams.hires_steps,
   448→        requestParams.additional_loras,
   449→        lorasParam.additional_loras,
   450→      );
   451→
   452→      const taskParamsToSend = composeTaskParams({
   453→        source: requestParams,
   454→        baseParams: buildImageGenerationBaseParams(requestParams, taskId, finalResolution),
   455→        segments: [lorasParam, referenceParams, hiresOverride],
   456→        mappedFields: [
   457→          {
   458→            from: 'shot_id',
   459→            include: (value) => isNonEmptyString(value),
   460→          },
   461→          { from: 'lightning_lora_strength_phase_1' },
   462→          { from: 'lightning_lora_strength_phase_2' },
   463→        ],
   464→      });
   465→
   466→      return composeTaskRequest({
   467→        source: requestParams,
   468→        taskType,
   469→        params: taskParamsToSend,
   470→      });
   471→    },
   472→  });
   473→}

   198→  validateRequiredFields(params, [
   199→    'project_id'
   200→  ]);
   201→
   202→  const clipSource = params.clip_source;
   203→  const clipSequence = buildClipSequenceFromSource(clipSource);
   204→
   205→  if (clipSequence.length < 2) {
   206→    throw new TaskValidationError("At least two clips are required to create a join", 'clips');
   207→  }
   208→
   209→  clipSequence.forEach((clip, index) => {
   210→    try {
   211→      validateNonEmptyString(clip.url, `clips[${index}]`, `Clip ${index + 1} URL`);
   212→    } catch {
   213→      throw new TaskValidationError(`Clip at position ${index} is missing a URL`, 'clips');
   214→    }
   215→  });
   216→
   217→  const joinsCount = clipSequence.length - 1;
   218→
   219→  if (params.per_join_settings && params.per_join_settings.length > joinsCount) {
   220→    throw new TaskValidationError(
   221→      "per_join_settings length cannot exceed the number of joins",
   222→      'per_join_settings'
   223→    );
   224→  }
   225→
   226→  const videoEdit = params.video_edit;
   227→  if (params.mode === 'video_edit' && !videoEdit) {
   228→    throw new TaskValidationError(
   229→      "video_edit config is required when mode is video_edit",
   230→      'mode',
   231→    );
   232→  }
   233→  if (videoEdit && !videoEdit.source_video_url) {
   234→    throw new TaskValidationError(
   235→      "video_edit.source_video_url is required when video_edit config is provided",
   236→      'video_edit',
   237→    );
   238→  }
   239→  if (params.mode !== 'video_edit' && videoEdit) {
   240→    throw new TaskValidationError(
   241→      "video_edit config can only be provided when mode is video_edit",
   242→      'mode',
   243→    );
   244→  }
   245→  if (params.mode === 'multi_clip' && clipSource.kind !== 'clips') {
   246→    throw new TaskValidationError(
   247→      "clip_source.kind must be clips when mode is multi_clip",
   248→      'mode',
   249→    );
   250→  }
   251→
   252→  const joinMode: JoinMode = params.mode === 'video_edit'
   253→    ? 'video_edit_join'
   254→    : 'multi_clip_join';
   255→
   256→  return {
   257→    clipSequence,
   258→    clipSourceKind: clipSource.kind,
   259→    joinMode,
   260→    videoEdit,
   261→  };
   262→}
   263→
   264→/**
   265→ * Builds the orchestrator payload for join clips
   266→ * 
   267→ * @param params - Raw join clips parameters
   268→ * @param clipSequence - Normalized list of clips in order
   269→ * @param runId - Generated run ID
   270→ * @param orchestratorTaskId - Generated orchestrator task ID
   271→ * @returns Processed orchestrator payload
   272→ */
   273→function buildJoinClipsPayload(
   274→  params: CanonicalJoinClipsTaskInput,
   275→  normalized: NormalizedJoinClipsParams,
   276→  runId: string,
   277→  orchestratorTaskId: string
   278→): Record<string, unknown> {
   279→  const clipSequence = normalized.clipSequence;
   280→  // Use provided phase config (advanced mode) or build from LoRAs (basic mode)
   281→  const phaseConfig = params.phase_config || buildJoinClipsPhaseConfig(params.loras || []);
   282→  
   283→  const orchestratorDetails: Record<string, unknown> = {
   284→    orchestrator_task_id: orchestratorTaskId,
   285→    clip_list: clipSequence.map(clip => ({
   286→      url: clip.url,
   287→      ...(clip.name ? { name: clip.name } : {}),
   288→    })),
   289→    run_id: runId,
   290→    shot_id: params.shot_id ?? undefined, // For "Visit Shot" button in TasksPane
   291→    prompt: params.prompt ?? TASK_DEFAULTS.prompt,
   292→    gap_frame_count: params.gap_frame_count ?? TASK_DEFAULTS.gap_frame_count,
   293→    context_frame_count: params.context_frame_count ?? TASK_DEFAULTS.context_frame_count,
   294→    replace_mode: params.replace_mode ?? TASK_DEFAULTS.replace_mode,
   295→    keep_bridging_images: params.keep_bridging_images, // Optional, defaults to undefined (backend handles default)
   296→    enhance_prompt: params.enhance_prompt ?? TASK_DEFAULTS.enhance_prompt,
   297→    model: params.model ?? TASK_DEFAULTS.model,
   298→    num_inference_steps: params.num_inference_steps ?? TASK_DEFAULTS.num_inference_steps,
   299→    guidance_scale: params.guidance_scale ?? TASK_DEFAULTS.guidance_scale,
   300→    seed: params.seed ?? TASK_DEFAULTS.seed,
   301→    negative_prompt: params.negative_prompt ?? TASK_DEFAULTS.negative_prompt,
   302→    priority: params.priority ?? TASK_DEFAULTS.priority,
   303→    parent_generation_id: params.parent_generation_id,
   304→    // UNIFIED: Always include phase_config and advanced_mode for consistent backend processing
   305→    phase_config: phaseConfig,
   306→    advanced_mode: true,
   307→    // Motion settings for UI state restoration
   308→    motion_mode: params.motion_mode ?? TASK_DEFAULTS.motion_mode,
   309→    selected_phase_preset_id: params.selected_phase_preset_id ?? TASK_DEFAULTS.selected_phase_preset_id,
   310→  };
   311→
   312→  assignMappedPayloadFields(orchestratorDetails, params, [
   313→    { from: 'resolution' },
   314→    { from: 'fps' },
   315→    { from: 'use_input_video_resolution' },
   316→    { from: 'use_input_video_fps' },
   317→    { from: 'audio_url' },
   318→  ]);
   319→
   320→  assignMappedPayloadFields(orchestratorDetails, params, [
   321→    {
   322→      from: 'vid2vid_init_strength',
   323→      include: (value) => typeof value === 'number' && value > 0,
   324→    },
   325→  ]);
   326→
   327→  if (params.loop_first_clip) {
   328→    orchestratorDetails.loop_first_clip = true;
   329→  }
   330→
   331→  // Pass based_on for variant creation when looping a clip from "Add to Join"
   332→  if (params.based_on) {
   333→    orchestratorDetails.based_on = params.based_on;
   334→  }
   335→
   336→  // Keep additional_loras for backward compatibility, but LoRAs are now primarily in phase_config
   337→  if (params.loras && params.loras.length > 0) {
   338→    orchestratorDetails.additional_loras = mapPathLorasToStrengthRecord(params.loras);
   339→  }
   340→  
   341→  // Video edit mode - for regenerating portions of a single video
   342→  if (normalized.videoEdit) {
   343→    orchestratorDetails.video_edit_mode = true;
   344→    orchestratorDetails.source_video_url = normalized.videoEdit.source_video_url;
   345→    orchestratorDetails.source_video_fps = normalized.videoEdit.source_video_fps;
   346→    orchestratorDetails.source_video_duration = normalized.videoEdit.source_video_duration;
   347→    orchestratorDetails.source_video_total_frames = normalized.videoEdit.source_video_total_frames;
   348→    orchestratorDetails.portions_to_regenerate = normalized.videoEdit.portions_to_regenerate;
   349→  }
   350→
   351→  const totalJoins = Math.max(clipSequence.length - 1, 0);
   352→  if (totalJoins > 0) {
   353→    const perJoinOverrides: Record<string, unknown>[] = [];
   354→    let hasOverrides = false;
   355→
   356→    for (let index = 0; index < totalJoins; index++) {
   357→      const joinSettings = buildJoinOverrideRecord(params.per_join_settings?.[index]);
   358→
   359→      if (Object.keys(joinSettings).length > 0) {
   360→        hasOverrides = true;
   361→        perJoinOverrides.push(joinSettings);
   362→      } else {
   363→        perJoinOverrides.push({});
   364→      }
   365→    }
   366→
   367→    if (hasOverrides) {
   368→      orchestratorDetails.per_join_settings = perJoinOverrides;
   369→    }
   370→  }
   371→
   372→  const resolutionDisplay = params.resolution
   373→    ? `${params.resolution[0]}x${params.resolution[1]}`
   374→    : undefined;
   375→
   376→  const joinMode = normalized.joinMode;
   377→
   378→  const perJoinOverridesCount = params.per_join_settings?.filter((override) =>
   379→    !!override && Object.keys(override).length > 0
   380→  ).length ?? 0;
   381→
   382→  const familyContract = buildJoinClipsFamilyContract({
   383→    mode: joinMode,
   384→    runId,
   385→    clipUrls: clipSequence.map((clip) => clip.url),
   386→    overridesCount: perJoinOverridesCount,
   387→    hasAudio: Boolean(params.audio_url),
   388→  });
   389→
   390→  const payload = composeTaskFamilyPayload({
   391→    taskFamily: 'join_clips',
   392→    orchestratorDetails,
   393→    orchestrationInput: {
   394→      taskFamily: 'join_clips',
   395→      orchestratorTaskId,
   396→      runId,
   397→      parentGenerationId: params.parent_generation_id,
   398→      shotId: params.shot_id,
   399→      basedOn: params.based_on,
   400→      generationRouting: 'orchestrator',
   401→      siblingLookup: 'run_id',
   402→    },
   403→    taskViewInput: {
   404→      inputImages: clipSequence.map((clip) => clip.url),
   405→      prompt: params.prompt,
   406→      negativePrompt: params.negative_prompt,
   407→      modelName: params.model,
   408→      resolution: resolutionDisplay,
   409→    },
   410→    familyContract,
   411→  });
   412→
   413→  return {
   414→    ...payload,
   415→    parent_generation_id: params.parent_generation_id,
   416→    // Only include tool_type if explicitly passed (Join Clips page passes it, ShotEditor doesn't)
   417→    ...(params.tool_type && { tool_type: params.tool_type }),
   418→  };
   419→}
   420→
   421→/**
   422→ * Creates a join clips task using the unified approach
   423→ * 
   424→ * @param params - Join clips task parameters
   425→ * @returns Promise resolving to the created task
   426→ */
   427→export async function createCanonicalJoinClipsTask(
   428→  params: CanonicalJoinClipsTaskInput,
   429→): Promise<TaskCreationResult> {
   430→  return runTaskCreationPipeline({
   431→    params,
   432→    context: 'JoinClips',
   433→    buildTaskRequest: (requestParams) => {
   434→      const normalized = normalizeJoinClipsParams(requestParams);
   435→      const orchestratorTaskId = generateTaskId("join_clips_orchestrator");
   436→      const runId = requestParams.run_id ?? generateRunId();
   437→      const orchestratorPayload = buildJoinClipsPayload(
   438→        requestParams,
   439→        normalized,
   440→        runId,
   441→        orchestratorTaskId,
   442→      );
   443→
   444→      return composeTaskRequest({
   445→        source: requestParams,
   446→        taskType: 'join_clips_orchestrator',
   447→        params: orchestratorPayload,
   448→      });
   449→    },
   450→  });
   451→}
   452→
   453→// TaskValidationError is used internally - import from taskCreation.ts if needed externally
   454→

1→export type PromptAssemblyPolicy = 'batch_comma' | 'legacy_batch_comma' | 'segment_space';
     2→
     3→const POLICY_DELIMITER: Record<PromptAssemblyPolicy, string> = {
     4→  batch_comma: ', ',
     5→  legacy_batch_comma: ', ',
     6→  segment_space: ' ',
     7→};
     8→
     9→function normalizePart(part: string | null | undefined): string {
    10→  return (part ?? '').trim();
    11→}
    12→
    13→/**
    14→ * Compose prompt fragments with an explicit normalization + delimiter policy.
    15→ * Keeping the policy named at call sites prevents hidden drift between paths.
    16→ */
    17→export function joinPromptParts(
    18→  parts: Array<string | null | undefined>,
    19→  policy: PromptAssemblyPolicy,
    20→): string {
    21→  const delimiter = POLICY_DELIMITER[policy];
    22→  return parts
    23→    .map(normalizePart)
    24→    .filter(Boolean)
    25→    .join(delimiter);
    26→}
    27→

1→/**
     2→ * VideoTravelSettingsProvider - Centralized settings context for Video Travel tool
     3→ *
     4→ * This provider owns all shot-specific settings state, making it accessible to
     5→ * any child component without prop drilling. Settings are persisted via useShotSettings.
     6→ *
     7→ * Architecture:
     8→ * - Wraps useShotSettings (state + persistence)
     9→ * - Wraps useVideoTravelSettingsHandlers (all update handlers)
    10→ * - Exposes focused hooks for each settings domain
    11→ *
    12→ * Usage:
    13→ * ```tsx
    14→ * // In VideoTravelToolPage
    15→ * <VideoTravelSettingsProvider projectId={projectId} shotId={shotId}>
    16→ *   <ShotSettingsEditor />
    17→ * </VideoTravelSettingsProvider>
    18→ *
    19→ * // In any child component
    20→ * const { prompt, setPrompt } = usePromptSettings();
    21→ * const { motionMode, setMotionMode } = useMotionSettings();
    22→ * ```
    23→ */

    45→  isDirty: boolean;
    46→  isLoading: boolean;

    82→}
    83→
    84→export const VideoTravelSettingsProvider: React.FC<VideoTravelSettingsProviderProps> = ({
    85→  projectId,
    86→  shotId,
    87→  selectedShot,
    88→  availableLoras,
    89→  updateShotMode,
    90→  children,
    91→}) => {
    92→  // Core settings hook - manages state + persistence
    93→  const shotSettings = useShotSettings(shotId, projectId);
    94→
    95→  // Create ref for handlers (they need ref to avoid recreation)
    96→  const shotSettingsRef = useRef(shotSettings);
    97→  shotSettingsRef.current = shotSettings;
    98→
    99→  // All handlers
   100→  const handlers = useVideoTravelSettingsHandlers({
   101→    shotSettingsRef,
   102→    currentShotId: shotId || null,
   103→    selectedShot,
   104→    updateShotMode,
   105→  });
   106→
   107→  // Memoize context value
   108→  const contextValue = useMemo<VideoTravelSettingsContextValue>(() => ({
   109→    settings: shotSettings.settings,
   110→    status: shotSettings.status,
   111→    isDirty: shotSettings.isDirty,
   112→    isLoading: shotSettings.status === 'loading' || shotSettings.status === 'idle',
   113→    shotId: shotSettings.shotId,
   114→    projectId: projectId || null,
   115→    handlers,
   116→    updateField: shotSettings.updateField,
   117→    updateFields: shotSettings.updateFields,
   118→    save: shotSettings.save,
   119→    saveImmediate: shotSettings.saveImmediate,
   120→    availableLoras,
   121→  }), [
   122→    shotSettings.settings,
   123→    shotSettings.status,
   124→    shotSettings.isDirty,
   125→    shotSettings.shotId,
   126→    shotSettings.updateField,
   127→    shotSettings.updateFields,
   128→    shotSettings.save,
   129→    shotSettings.saveImmediate,
   130→    projectId,
   131→    handlers,
   132→    availableLoras,
   133→  ]);
   134→
   135→  return (
   136→    <VideoTravelSettingsContext.Provider value={contextValue}>
   137→      {children}
   138→    </VideoTravelSettingsContext.Provider>
   139→  );
   140→};
   141→

   146→export function useVideoTravelSettings(): VideoTravelSettingsContextValue {

   168→    enhancePrompt: settings.enhancePrompt,

   172→    setTextAfterPrompts: handlers.handleTextAfterPromptsChange,

   175→}
   176→

1→import { createTask, type BaseTaskParams, type TaskCreationResult } from '@/shared/lib/taskCreation';
     2→import { rethrowTaskCreationError } from './taskCreationError';
     3→
     4→interface TaskCreationPipelineConfig<TParams, TResult = TaskCreationResult> {
     5→  params: TParams;
     6→  context: string;
     7→  validate?: (params: TParams) => void;
     8→  buildTaskRequest: (params: TParams) => Promise<BaseTaskParams> | BaseTaskParams;
     9→  onCreated?: (result: TaskCreationResult, params: TParams) => Promise<TResult> | TResult;
    10→}
    11→
    12→export async function runTaskCreationPipeline<TParams, TResult = TaskCreationResult>(
    13→  config: TaskCreationPipelineConfig<TParams, TResult>,
    14→): Promise<TResult> {
    15→  const { params, context, validate, buildTaskRequest, onCreated } = config;
    16→
    17→  try {
    18→    validate?.(params);
    19→    const taskRequest = await buildTaskRequest(params);
    20→    const createdTask = await createTask(taskRequest);
    21→    if (!onCreated) {
    22→      return createdTask as TResult;
    23→    }
    24→    return await onCreated(createdTask, params);
    25→  } catch (error) {
    26→    rethrowTaskCreationError(error, { context, showToast: false });
    27→  }
    28→}
    29→

1→import type { BaseTaskParams } from '../taskCreation';
     2→import {
     3→  assignMappedPayloadFields,
     4→  type PayloadFieldMapping,
     5→} from '../taskCreation/payloadMapping';
     6→
     7→type PayloadSegment = Record<string, unknown> | null | undefined;
     8→
     9→interface ComposeTaskParamsInput<TSource extends object> {
    10→  source: TSource;
    11→  baseParams?: Record<string, unknown>;
    12→  segments?: readonly PayloadSegment[];
    13→  mappedFields?: readonly PayloadFieldMapping<TSource>[];
    14→}
    15→
    16→interface ComposeTaskRequestInput<TSource extends { project_id: string }> {
    17→  source: TSource;
    18→  taskType: string;
    19→  params: Record<string, unknown>;
    20→}
    21→
    22→/**
    23→ * Shared task-payload composition primitive used across task families.
    24→ */
    25→export function composeTaskParams<TSource extends object>(
    26→  input: ComposeTaskParamsInput<TSource>,
    27→): Record<string, unknown> {
    28→  const composed: Record<string, unknown> = {
    29→    ...(input.baseParams ?? {}),
    30→  };
    31→
    32→  for (const segment of input.segments ?? []) {
    33→    if (segment && typeof segment === 'object') {
    34→      Object.assign(composed, segment);
    35→    }
    36→  }
    37→
    38→  if (input.mappedFields && input.mappedFields.length > 0) {
    39→    assignMappedPayloadFields(composed, input.source, input.mappedFields);
    40→  }
    41→
    42→  return composed;
    43→}
    44→
    45→export function composeTaskRequest<TSource extends { project_id: string }>(
    46→  input: ComposeTaskRequestInput<TSource>,
    47→): BaseTaskParams {
    48→  return {
    49→    project_id: input.source.project_id,
    50→    task_type: input.taskType,
    51→    params: input.params,
    52→  };
    53→}

1→export type OperationFailurePolicy = 'fail_closed' | 'fail_open' | 'degrade' | 'best_effort';
     2→
     3→export interface OperationSuccess<T> {
     4→  ok: true;
     5→  value: T;
     6→  policy: OperationFailurePolicy;
     7→  recoverable: false;
     8→}
     9→
    10→export interface OperationFailure {
    11→  ok: false;
    12→  error: Error;
    13→  message: string;
    14→  recoverable: boolean;
    15→  policy: OperationFailurePolicy;
    16→  errorCode: string;
    17→  cause?: unknown;
    18→}
    19→
    20→export type OperationResult<T> = OperationSuccess<T> | OperationFailure;
    21→
    22→export class OperationResultError extends Error {
    23→  errorCode: string;
    24→  policy: OperationFailurePolicy;
    25→  recoverable: boolean;
    26→  cause?: unknown;
    27→
    28→  constructor(options: {
    29→    message: string;
    30→    errorCode: string;
    31→    policy: OperationFailurePolicy;
    32→    recoverable: boolean;
    33→    cause?: unknown;
    34→    sourceError?: Error;
    35→  }) {
    36→    super(options.message);
    37→    this.name = 'OperationResultError';
    38→    this.errorCode = options.errorCode;
    39→    this.policy = options.policy;
    40→    this.recoverable = options.recoverable;
    41→    this.cause = options.cause;
    42→
    43→    // Preserve the original stack for easier debugging when available.
    44→    if (options.sourceError?.stack) {
    45→      this.stack = options.sourceError.stack;
    46→    }
    47→  }
    48→}
    49→
    50→interface OperationSuccessOptions {
    51→  policy?: OperationFailurePolicy;
    52→}
    53→
    54→interface OperationFailureOptions {
    55→  policy?: OperationFailurePolicy;
    56→  recoverable?: boolean;
    57→  errorCode?: string;
    58→  message?: string;
    59→  cause?: unknown;
    60→}
    61→
    62→export function operationSuccess<T>(value: T, options?: OperationSuccessOptions): OperationSuccess<T> {
    63→  return {
    64→    ok: true,
    65→    value,
    66→    policy: options?.policy ?? 'best_effort',
    67→    recoverable: false,
    68→  };
    69→}
    70→
    71→export function operationFailure(error: unknown, options?: OperationFailureOptions): OperationFailure {
    72→  const normalizedError = error instanceof Error ? error : new Error(String(error));
    73→  return {
    74→    ok: false,
    75→    error: normalizedError,
    76→    message: options?.message ?? normalizedError.message,
    77→    recoverable: options?.recoverable ?? true,
    78→    policy: options?.policy ?? 'best_effort',
    79→    errorCode: options?.errorCode ?? 'operation_failed',
    80→    ...(options?.cause !== undefined ? { cause: options.cause } : {}),
    81→  };
    82→}
    83→
    84→/**
    85→ * Convert a structured operation failure into an Error while preserving machine-readable metadata.
    86→ */
    87→export function toOperationResultError(failure: OperationFailure): OperationResultError {
    88→  return new OperationResultError({
    89→    message: failure.message,
    90→    errorCode: failure.errorCode,
    91→    policy: failure.policy,
    92→    recoverable: failure.recoverable,
    93→    cause: failure.cause,
    94→    sourceError: failure.error,
    95→  });
    96→}
    97→

1→import { debugConfig } from '@/shared/lib/debug/debugConfig';
     2→import type { TrackableImage, TrackerLimits } from './types';
     3→
     4→const getTrackerConfig = (): TrackerLimits => {
     5→  const isMobile = typeof window !== 'undefined' && window.innerWidth <= 768;
     6→  const hasLowMemory =
     7→    typeof navigator !== 'undefined' &&
     8→    'deviceMemory' in navigator &&
     9→    (navigator as { deviceMemory?: number }).deviceMemory !== undefined &&
    10→    (navigator as { deviceMemory: number }).deviceMemory <= 4;
    11→
    12→  if (isMobile || hasLowMemory) {
    13→    return { maxImages: 100, maxUrls: 150 };
    14→  }
    15→  return { maxImages: 300, maxUrls: 500 };
    16→};
    17→
    18→const loadedImagesById = new Map<string, boolean>();
    19→
    20→const loadedImagesByUrl = new Map<
    21→  string,
    22→  { loadedAt: number; width?: number; height?: number; element?: HTMLImageElement }
    23→>();
    24→
    25→const shouldLogTrackerDebug = (): boolean =>
    26→  import.meta.env.DEV && debugConfig.isEnabled('imageLoading');
    27→
    28→/**
    29→ * Evict oldest entries from a Map until it's under the limit.
    30→ * Maps maintain insertion order, so we delete from the beginning.
    31→ */
    32→const evictOldestEntries = <K, V>(
    33→  map: Map<K, V>,
    34→  maxSize: number,
    35→  name: string
    36→): number => {
    37→  if (map.size <= maxSize) return 0;
    38→
    39→  const toEvict = map.size - maxSize;
    40→  const keys = Array.from(map.keys()).slice(0, toEvict);
    41→
    42→  keys.forEach((key) => map.delete(key));
    43→
    44→  if (shouldLogTrackerDebug()) {
    45→    console.log(
    46→      `[ImageLoadTracker] Evicted ${toEvict} oldest entries from ${name}, new size: ${map.size}`
    47→    );
    48→  }
    49→  return toEvict;
    50→};
    51→
    52→const enforceLoadTrackerLimits = (): void => {
    53→  const config = getTrackerConfig();
    54→  evictOldestEntries(loadedImagesById, config.maxImages, 'loadedImagesById');
    55→  evictOldestEntries(loadedImagesByUrl, config.maxUrls, 'loadedImagesByUrl');
    56→};
    57→
    58→export const setImageLoadStatus = (
    59→  image: TrackableImage,
    60→  isLoaded: boolean = true
    61→): void => {
    62→  const imageId = image.id;
    63→  if (!imageId) {
    64→    return;
    65→  }
    66→
    67→  // Update tracker
    68→  loadedImagesById.set(imageId, isLoaded);
    69→
    70→  // Keep legacy field in sync while older call sites are still present.
    71→  image.__memoryCached = isLoaded;
    72→
    73→  // Enforce limits in coarse batches to avoid per-write overhead.
    74→  if (isLoaded && loadedImagesById.size % 50 === 0) {
    75→    enforceLoadTrackerLimits();
    76→  }
    77→};
    78→
    79→const removeLoadedImages = (imageIds: string[]): number => {
    80→  let removedCount = 0;
    81→
    82→  imageIds.forEach((imageId) => {
    83→    if (loadedImagesById.has(imageId)) {
    84→      loadedImagesById.delete(imageId);
    85→      removedCount++;
    86→    }
    87→  });
    88→
    89→  return removedCount;
    90→};
    91→
    92→export const clearLoadedImages = (images: Array<{ id: string }>): number => {
    93→  const imageIds = images.map((img) => img.id).filter((id) => id);
    94→
    95→  return removeLoadedImages(imageIds);
    96→};
    97→
    98→export const clearAllLoadedImages = (
    99→  reason: string = 'project switch'
   100→): number => {
   101→  const prevSize = loadedImagesById.size;
   102→  loadedImagesById.clear();
   103→  loadedImagesByUrl.clear();
   104→
   105→  if (shouldLogTrackerDebug()) {
   106→    console.log(
   107→      `[ImageLoadTracker] Cleared all for ${reason}, removed ${prevSize} entries`
   108→    );
   109→  }
   110→  return prevSize;
   111→};
   112→
   113→export const hasLoadedImage = (urlOrImage: string | TrackableImage): boolean => {
   114→  if (typeof urlOrImage === 'string') {
   115→    return loadedImagesByUrl.has(urlOrImage);
   116→  }
   117→
   118→  const imageId = urlOrImage?.id;
   119→  if (!imageId) {
   120→    return false;
   121→  }
   122→
   123→  const isLoaded = loadedImagesById.get(imageId) === true;
   124→
   125→  if (isLoaded && urlOrImage.__memoryCached !== true) {
   126→    urlOrImage.__memoryCached = true;
   127→  }
   128→
   129→  return isLoaded;
   130→};
   131→
   132→export const markImageLoaded = (
   133→  urlOrImage: string | TrackableImage,
   134→  metadata?: { width?: number; height?: number; element?: HTMLImageElement }
   135→): void => {
   136→  if (typeof urlOrImage === 'string') {
   137→    loadedImagesByUrl.set(urlOrImage, {
   138→      loadedAt: Date.now(),
   139→      ...metadata,
   140→    });
   141→    if (loadedImagesByUrl.size % 50 === 0) {
   142→      enforceLoadTrackerLimits();
   143→    }
   144→    return;
   145→  }
   146→
   147→  setImageLoadStatus(urlOrImage, true);
   148→};
   149→
   150→export const getLoadTrackerStats = (): {
   151→  byId: number;
   152→  byUrl: number;
   153→  limits: TrackerLimits;
   154→} => {
   155→  const config = getTrackerConfig();
   156→  return {
   157→    byId: loadedImagesById.size,
   158→    byUrl: loadedImagesByUrl.size,
   159→    limits: config,
   160→  };
   161→};
   162→
   163→export const getImageElement = (url: string): HTMLImageElement | undefined => {
   164→  return loadedImagesByUrl.get(url)?.element;
   165→};
   166→

> DEVELOPER

You are a blind code quality reviewer. Your job is to evaluate the codebase at /Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh for specific quality dimensions. You must explore the codebase thoroughly and produce findings (defects only, never positive observations).

## Your Dimensions

### naming_quality
Description: Function/variable/file names that communicate intent
Look for:
- Generic verbs that reveal nothing: process, handle, do, run, manage
- Name/behavior mismatch: getX() that mutates state, isX() returning non-boolean
- Vocabulary divergence from codebase norms
- Abbreviations inconsistent with codebase conventions
Skip:
- Standard framework names (render, mount, useEffect)
- Short-lived loop variables (i, j, k)
- Well-known abbreviations matching codebase convention (ctx, req, res)

### logic_clarity
Description: Control flow and logic that provably does what it claims
Look for:
- Identical if/else or ternary branches (same code on both sides)
- Dead code paths: code after unconditional return/raise/throw/break
- Always-true or always-false conditions
- Redundant null/undefined checks on values that cannot be null
- Async functions that never await
- Boolean expressions that simplify: `if x: return True else: return False`
Skip:
- Deliberate no-op branches with explanatory comments
- Framework lifecycle methods that must be async by contract
- Guard clauses that are defensive by design

### type_safety
Description: Type annotations that match runtime behavior
Look for:
- Return type annotations that don't cover all code paths
- Parameters typed as X but called with Y
- Union types that could be narrowed
- Missing annotations on public API functions
- Type: ignore comments without explanation
Skip:
- Untyped private helpers in well-typed modules
- Test code with loose typing

### contract_coherence
Description: Functions and modules that honor their stated contracts
Look for:
- Return type annotation lies: declared type doesn't match all return paths
- Docstring/signature divergence
- Functions named getX that mutate state
- Module-level API inconsistency: some exports follow a pattern, one doesn't
Skip:
- Protocol/interface stubs
- Test helpers

### error_consistency
Description: Consistent error strategies, preserved context, predictable failure modes
Look for:
- Mixed error strategies: some functions throw, others return null, others use Result types
- Error context lost at boundaries: catch-and-rethrow without wrapping original
- Silent error swallowing: catches that log but don't propagate or recover
- Missing error handling on I/O boundaries
Skip:
- Intentional error boundaries at top-level handlers
- Different strategies for different layers

### convention_outlier
Description: Naming convention drift, inconsistent file organization, style islands
Look for:
- Naming convention drift: snake_case functions in a camelCase codebase or vice versa
- Inconsistent file organization: some dirs use index files, others don't
- Mixed export patterns across sibling modules
- Style islands: one directory uses a completely different pattern than the rest
Skip:
- Intentional variation for different module types
- Third-party code or generated files

### authorization_consistency
Description: Auth/permission patterns consistently applied across the codebase
Look for:
- Route handlers with [REDACTED] on some siblings but not others
- RLS enabled on some tables but not siblings in the same domain
- Permission strings as magic literals instead of shared constants
- Mixed trust boundaries: some endpoints validate user input, siblings don't
Skip:
- Public routes explicitly documented as unauthenticated
- Internal service-to-service calls behind network-level auth

## Rules
1. Only emit findings you are confident about. When unsure, skip entirely.
2. Every finding MUST include at least one entry in related_files as evidence.
3. Every finding MUST include a concrete, actionable suggestion.
4. Be specific, not vague.
5. Calibrate confidence: high = any senior eng would agree, medium = most would agree, low = reasonable engineers might disagree.
6. FINDINGS MUST BE DEFECTS ONLY. Never report positive observations.
7. If a dimension has no defects, give it a high assessment score (0-100) and return zero findings.
8. Score from evidence, not from a target.

## Exploring the codebase
Start by reading structure.md. Then explore src/shared/hooks/, src/shared/lib/, src/tools/, and supabase/functions/ to check naming patterns, logic issues, type safety, error handling consistency, and auth patterns. Look broadly across the codebase for convention outliers.

    72→
    73→## Core Concepts
    74→
    75→### Tools
    76→Tools live in `/src/tools/{tool-name}/` following a consistent structure. See [adding_new_tool.md](docs/structure_detail/adding_new_tool.md).
    77→
    78→**Active tools:** Image Generation, Video Travel, Animate Characters, Edit Images, Edit Video, Join Clips, Training Data Helper
    79→
    80→### Shots & Generations
    81→- **Generations** = gallery items (images/videos produced by AI tasks)
    82→- **Shots** = containers that organize generations into a timeline
    83→- **`shot_generations`** = join table with position + metadata (pair prompts, timeline frame)
    84→- Data access: `useShotImages(shotId)` → see [data_fetching.md](docs/structure_detail/data_fetching.md)
    85→
    86→### Settings Resolution
    87→Priority: **shot → project → user → defaults**. See [settings_system.md](docs/structure_detail/settings_system.md).
    88→
    89→### Task System
    90→Async queue for AI workloads: client creates task → DB trigger → worker polls → Edge Function completes.
    91→See [task_worker_lifecycle.md](docs/structure_detail/task_worker_lifecycle.md).
    92→
    93→### Realtime
    94→Smart polling + Supabase realtime subscriptions. Connected = no polling; disconnected = 15s fallback.
    95→See [realtime_system.md](docs/structure_detail/realtime_system.md).
    96→

    98→
    99→## Key Utilities

1→/**
     2→ * useVariants Hook
     3→ *
     4→ * Centralized hook for fetching and managing variants for a generation.
     5→ * Allows switching between variants and setting the primary variant.
     6→ * Supports realtime updates via RealtimeProvider.
     7→ *
     8→ * Used by: MediaLightbox, InlineEditView, and other components that display variants.
     9→ */
    10→
    11→import { useState, useCallback, useMemo, useEffect } from 'react';
    12→import { useQuery, useMutation, useQueryClient } from '@tanstack/react-query';
    13→import { getSupabaseClient as supabase } from '@/integrations/supabase/client';
    14→import { invalidateVariantChange } from '@/shared/hooks/invalidation/useGenerationInvalidation';
    15→import { normalizeAndPresentError } from '@/shared/lib/errorHandling/runtimeError';
    16→import { generationQueryKeys } from '@/shared/lib/queryKeys/generations';
    17→import { useAppEventListener } from '@/shared/lib/typedEvents';
    18→
    19→/**
    20→ * A variant of a generation (from generation_variants table)
    21→ */
    22→export interface GenerationVariant {
    23→  id: string;
    24→  generation_id: string;
    25→  location: string;
    26→  thumbnail_url: string | null;
    27→  params: Record<string, unknown> | null;
    28→  is_primary: boolean;
    29→  starred: boolean;
    30→  variant_type: string | null;
    31→  name: string | null;
    32→  created_at: string;
    33→  viewed_at: string | null;
    34→}
    35→
    36→/**
    37→ * Return type for useVariants hook
    38→ */
    39→interface UseVariantsReturn {
    40→  variants: GenerationVariant[];
    41→  primaryVariant: GenerationVariant | null;
    42→  activeVariant: GenerationVariant | null;
    43→  isLoading: boolean;
    44→  error: Error | null;
    45→  refetch: () => void;
    46→  setActiveVariantId: (variantId: string | null) => void;
    47→  setPrimaryVariant: (variantId: string) => Promise<void>;
    48→  deleteVariant: (variantId: string) => Promise<void>;
    49→}
    50→
    51→interface UseVariantsProps {
    52→  generationId: string | null;
    53→  enabled?: boolean;
    54→}
    55→
    56→export const useVariants = ({
    57→  generationId,
    58→  enabled = true,
    59→}: UseVariantsProps): UseVariantsReturn => {
    60→  const queryClient = useQueryClient();
    61→  const [activeVariantId, setActiveVariantIdInternal] = useState<string | null>(null);
    62→  
    63→  // Stable callback - no deps needed since we just forward to internal setter
    64→  const setActiveVariantId = useCallback((variantId: string | null) => {
    65→    setActiveVariantIdInternal(variantId);
    66→  }, []);
    67→
    68→  // Fetch variants for this generation
    69→  const {
    70→    data: variants = [],
    71→    isLoading,
    72→    error,
    73→    refetch,
    74→  } = useQuery({
    75→    queryKey: generationId ? generationQueryKeys.variants(generationId) : ['generation-variants', null],
    76→    queryFn: async () => {
    77→      if (!generationId) return [];
    78→
    79→      const { data, error } = await supabase().from('generation_variants')
    80→        .select('*')
    81→        .eq('generation_id', generationId)
    82→        .order('created_at', { ascending: false });
    83→
    84→      if (error) {
    85→        console.error('[useVariants] Error fetching variants:', error);
    86→        throw error;
    87→      }
    88→
    89→      return (data || []) as GenerationVariant[];
    90→    },
    91→    enabled: enabled && !!generationId,
    92→    staleTime: 30000, // 30 seconds
    93→  });
    94→
    95→  // Listen for realtime variant changes and refetch when our generationId is affected
    96→  const handleVariantChange = useCallback((detail: { affectedGenerationIds: string[] }) => {
    97→    if (!generationId || !enabled) return;
    98→    const affectedIds = detail?.affectedGenerationIds || [];
    99→    if (affectedIds.includes(generationId)) {
   100→      refetch();
   101→    }
   102→  }, [generationId, enabled, refetch]);
   103→
   104→  useAppEventListener('realtime:variant-change-batch', handleVariantChange);
   105→
   106→  // Find the primary variant
   107→  const primaryVariant = useMemo(() => {
   108→    return variants.find((v) => v.is_primary) || null;
   109→  }, [variants]);
   110→
   111→  // Get the active variant (selected or primary, fallback to first variant)
   112→  const activeVariant = useMemo(() => {
   113→    if (activeVariantId) {
   114→      const found = variants.find((v) => v.id === activeVariantId);
   115→      if (found) {
   116→        return found;
   117→      }
   118→    }
   119→    // Fall back to primary, then first variant if no primary exists
   120→    return primaryVariant || variants[0] || null;
   121→  }, [variants, activeVariantId, primaryVariant]);
   122→
   123→  // Initialize active variant to primary (or first variant) when variants load
   124→  // NOTE: Using useEffect, not useMemo - side effects should not be in useMemo
   125→  useEffect(() => {
   126→    if (!activeVariantId && variants.length > 0) {
   127→      const variantToSelect = primaryVariant || variants[0];
   128→      if (variantToSelect) {
   129→        setActiveVariantIdInternal(variantToSelect.id);
   130→      }
   131→    }
   132→  }, [primaryVariant, variants, activeVariantId]);
   133→
   134→  // Mutation to set a variant as primary
   135→  const setPrimaryMutation = useMutation({
   136→    mutationFn: async (variantId: string) => {
   137→
   138→      // Update the variant to be primary
   139→      // The database trigger will handle unsetting the old primary
   140→      const { error } = await supabase().from('generation_variants')
   141→        .update({ is_primary: true })
   142→        .eq('id', variantId);
   143→
   144→      if (error) {
   145→        console.error('[useVariants] Error setting primary variant:', error);
   146→        throw error;
   147→      }
   148→
   149→      return variantId;
   150→    },
   151→    onSuccess: async (variantId) => {
   152→
   153→      // Invalidate caches using centralized function
   154→      if (generationId) {
   155→        await invalidateVariantChange(queryClient, {
   156→          generationId,
   157→          reason: 'set-primary-variant',
   158→        });
   159→      }
   160→
   161→      // SINGLE-SEGMENT PROPAGATION: If this is a child of a single-segment parent,
   162→      // also create a variant on the parent so the main generation updates
   163→      try {
   164→        // Get the promoted variant's location and thumbnail
   165→        const { data: promotedVariant } = await supabase().from('generation_variants')
   166→          .select('location, thumbnail_url, params')
   167→          .eq('id', variantId)
   168→          .single();
   169→
   170→        if (!promotedVariant || !generationId) return;
   171→
   172→        // Check if this generation is a child with a parent
   173→        const { data: generation } = await supabase().from('generations')
   174→          .select('is_child, parent_generation_id')
   175→          .eq('id', generationId)
   176→          .single();
   177→
   178→        if (!generation?.is_child || !generation?.parent_generation_id) return;
   179→
   180→        // Count how many children the parent has
   181→        const { count: childCount } = await supabase().from('generations')
   182→          .select('id', { count: 'exact', head: true })
   183→          .eq('parent_generation_id', generation.parent_generation_id)
   184→          .eq('is_child', true);
   185→
   186→        // Only propagate for single-segment parents
   187→        if (childCount !== 1) {
   188→          return;
   189→        }
   190→
   191→        // Create a new variant on the parent with the promoted video
   192→        // Exclude task-specific fields that shouldn't propagate to parent
   193→        const {
   194→          source_task_id: _sourceTaskId,
   195→          child_generation_id: _childGenId,
   196→          ...paramsToPropagate
   197→        } = (promotedVariant.params || {}) as Record<string, unknown>;
   198→
   199→        const { error: insertError } = await supabase().from('generation_variants')
   200→          .insert({
   201→            generation_id: generation.parent_generation_id,
   202→            location: promotedVariant.location,
   203→            thumbnail_url: promotedVariant.thumbnail_url,
   204→            is_primary: true, // DB trigger will unset old primary
   205→            variant_type: 'travel_segment',
   206→            params: {
   207→              ...paramsToPropagate,
   208→              propagated_from_child: generationId,
   209→              propagated_from_variant: variantId,
   210→            },
   211→          });
   212→
   213→        if (insertError) {
   214→          normalizeAndPresentError(insertError, { context: 'useVariants', showToast: false });
   215→        } else {
   216→          // Invalidate parent's variant cache
   217→          await invalidateVariantChange(queryClient, {
   218→            generationId: generation.parent_generation_id,
   219→            reason: 'single-segment-propagation',
   220→          });
   221→        }
   222→      } catch (err) {
   223→        console.error('[useVariants] Error in single-segment propagation:', err);
   224→        // Don't throw - this is a nice-to-have, not critical
   225→      }
   226→    },
   227→    onError: (error) => {
   228→      normalizeAndPresentError(error, { context: 'useVariants.setPrimaryVariant', toastTitle: 'Failed to set primary variant' });
   229→    },
   230→  });
   231→
   232→  const setPrimaryVariant = useCallback(
   233→    async (variantId: string) => {
   234→      await setPrimaryMutation.mutateAsync(variantId);
   235→    },
   236→    [setPrimaryMutation]
   237→  );
   238→
   239→  // Mutation to delete a variant
   240→  const deleteVariantMutation = useMutation({
   241→    mutationFn: async (variantId: string) => {
   242→
   243→      // Check if variant is primary - don't allow deleting primary
   244→      const variant = variants.find(v => v.id === variantId);
   245→      if (variant?.is_primary) {
   246→        throw new Error('Cannot delete the primary variant');
   247→      }
   248→
   249→      const { error } = await supabase().from('generation_variants')
   250→        .delete()
   251→        .eq('id', variantId);
   252→
   253→      if (error) {
   254→        console.error('[useVariants] Error deleting variant:', error);
   255→        throw error;
   256→      }
   257→
   258→      return variantId;
   259→    },
   260→    onSuccess: async (variantId) => {
   261→
   262→      // If deleted variant was active, switch to primary
   263→      if (activeVariantId === variantId) {
   264→        setActiveVariantId(primaryVariant?.id || null);
   265→      }
   266→
   267→      // Invalidate caches
   268→      if (generationId) {
   269→        await invalidateVariantChange(queryClient, {
   270→          generationId,
   271→          reason: 'delete-variant',
   272→        });
   273→      }
   274→    },
   275→    onError: (error) => {
   276→      normalizeAndPresentError(error, { context: 'useVariants.deleteVariant', toastTitle: 'Failed to delete variant' });
   277→    },
   278→  });
   279→
   280→  const deleteVariant = useCallback(
   281→    async (variantId: string) => {
   282→      await deleteVariantMutation.mutateAsync(variantId);
   283→    },
   284→    [deleteVariantMutation]
   285→  );
   286→
   287→  return {
   288→    variants,
   289→    primaryVariant,
   290→    activeVariant,
   291→    isLoading,
   292→    error: error as Error | null,
   293→    refetch,
   294→    setActiveVariantId,
   295→    setPrimaryVariant,
   296→    deleteVariant,
   297→  };
   298→};
   299→
