1→/**
     2→ * Centralized storage path utilities for Edge Functions
     3→ * 
     4→ * This is a copy of src/shared/lib/storagePaths.ts for use in Deno edge functions.
     5→ * Keep these in sync when making changes!
     6→ * 
     7→ * Path Structure:
     8→ *   {userId}/uploads/         - All media files (images + videos)
     9→ *   {userId}/thumbnails/      - All generated thumbnails
    10→ *   {userId}/tasks/{taskId}/  - Task/worker outputs via pre-signed URLs
    11→ */
    12→
    13→/**
    14→ * Generate a unique filename with timestamp and random string
    15→ */
    16→export function generateUniqueFilename(extension: string): string {
    17→  const timestamp = Date.now();
    18→  const randomStr = Math.random().toString(36).substring(2, 10);
    19→  return `${timestamp}-${randomStr}.${extension}`;
    20→}
    21→
    22→/**
    23→ * Generate a unique thumbnail filename
    24→ */
    25→export function generateThumbnailFilename(): string {
    26→  const timestamp = Date.now();
    27→  const randomStr = Math.random().toString(36).substring(2, 8);
    28→  return `thumb_${timestamp}_${randomStr}.jpg`;
    29→}
    30→
    31→/**
    32→ * Get file extension from filename, with MIME type fallback
    33→ */
    34→export function getFileExtension(
    35→  filename: string,
    36→  mimeType?: string,
    37→  defaultExt: string = 'bin'
    38→): string {
    39→  // Handle URLs and query/hash suffixes from signed object paths.
    40→  const cleanName = filename
    41→    .split('?')[0]
    42→    .split('#')[0]
    43→    .split('/')
    44→    .pop() ?? filename;
    45→  const dotIndex = cleanName.lastIndexOf('.');
    46→  if (dotIndex > 0 && dotIndex < cleanName.length - 1) {
    47→    return cleanName.slice(dotIndex + 1).toLowerCase();
    48→  }
    49→  
    50→  // Fallback to MIME type
    51→  if (mimeType) {
    52→    const mimeExt = mimeType.split('/')[1]?.split(';')[0]?.replace('jpeg', 'jpg');
    53→    if (mimeExt) return mimeExt;
    54→  }
    55→  
    56→  return defaultExt;
    57→}

   291→export function writeSegmentOverrides(
   292→  currentMetadata: Record<string, unknown> | null | undefined,
   293→  overrides: SegmentOverrides
   294→): Record<string, unknown> {
   295→  const metadata = { ...(currentMetadata ?? {}) };
   296→
   297→  // Start with existing segmentOverrides (merge, not replace)
   298→  const existingOverrides = (metadata.segmentOverrides ?? {}) as Record<string, unknown>;
   299→  const newOverrides = { ...existingOverrides };
   300→
   301→  // Update each field if present in overrides
   302→  // Use explicit undefined check so we can distinguish "not provided" from "set to value"
   303→  if (overrides.prompt !== undefined) {
   304→    newOverrides.prompt = overrides.prompt;
   305→  }
   306→  if (overrides.negativePrompt !== undefined) {
   307→    newOverrides.negativePrompt = overrides.negativePrompt;
   308→  }
   309→  if (overrides.motionMode !== undefined) {
   310→    newOverrides.motionMode = overrides.motionMode;
   311→  }
   312→  if (overrides.amountOfMotion !== undefined) {
   313→    newOverrides.amountOfMotion = overrides.amountOfMotion;
   314→  }
   315→  if (overrides.phaseConfig !== undefined) {
   316→    newOverrides.phaseConfig = overrides.phaseConfig;
   317→  }
   318→  if (overrides.selectedPhasePresetId !== undefined) {
   319→    newOverrides.selectedPhasePresetId = overrides.selectedPhasePresetId;
   320→  }
   321→  if (overrides.loras !== undefined) {
   322→    newOverrides.loras = overrides.loras;  // Preserve empty arrays to distinguish "no loras" from "use shot default"
   323→  }
   324→  if (overrides.numFrames !== undefined) {
   325→    newOverrides.numFrames = overrides.numFrames;
   326→  }
   327→  if (overrides.randomSeed !== undefined) {
   328→    newOverrides.randomSeed = overrides.randomSeed;
   329→  }
   330→  if (overrides.seed !== undefined) {
   331→    newOverrides.seed = overrides.seed;
   332→  }
   333→  // Structure video overrides
   334→  if (overrides.structureMotionStrength !== undefined) {
   335→    newOverrides.structureMotionStrength = overrides.structureMotionStrength;
   336→  }
   337→  if (overrides.structureTreatment !== undefined) {
   338→    newOverrides.structureTreatment = overrides.structureTreatment;
   339→  }
   340→  if (overrides.structureUni3cEndPercent !== undefined) {
   341→    newOverrides.structureUni3cEndPercent = overrides.structureUni3cEndPercent;
   342→  }
   343→  // Text before/after prompts
   344→  if (overrides.textBeforePrompts !== undefined) {
   345→    newOverrides.textBeforePrompts = overrides.textBeforePrompts;
   346→  }
   347→  if (overrides.textAfterPrompts !== undefined) {
   348→    newOverrides.textAfterPrompts = overrides.textAfterPrompts;
   349→  }
   350→
   351→  metadata.segmentOverrides = newOverrides;
   352→
   353→  // Clean up empty segmentOverrides
   354→  if (Object.keys(newOverrides).length === 0) {
   355→    delete metadata.segmentOverrides;
   356→  }
   357→
   358→  return metadata;
   359→}

    73→  if (!Number.isFinite(timestamp)) {
    74→    return false;
    75→  }
    76→  return now.getTime() > timestamp;

1→import { isPastRemovalTarget, type DeprecationPolicy } from '@/shared/lib/governance/deprecationPolicy';
     2→import {
     3→  normalizeAndPresentAndRethrow,
     4→  normalizeAndPresentError,
     5→} from '@/shared/lib/errorHandling/runtimeError';
     6→
     7→const signaledDeprecations = new Set<string>();
     8→
     9→interface DeprecationSignalOptions {
    10→  alias: string;
    11→  policy: DeprecationPolicy;
    12→  remediation?: string;
    13→  enforcement?: 'warn' | 'throw' | 'auto';
    14→}
    15→
    16→function resolveEnforcementMode(mode: DeprecationSignalOptions['enforcement']): 'warn' | 'throw' {
    17→  if (mode === 'warn' || mode === 'throw') {
    18→    return mode;
    19→  }
    20→
    21→  const metaEnv = typeof import.meta !== 'undefined'
    22→    ? (import.meta as unknown as { env?: Record<string, string | undefined> }).env
    23→    : undefined;
    24→  const nodeEnv = typeof process !== 'undefined' ? process.env?.NODE_ENV : undefined;
    25→  const isTestMode = nodeEnv === 'test' || metaEnv?.MODE === 'test' || metaEnv?.VITEST === 'true';
    26→  const explicit = metaEnv?.VITE_DEPRECATION_ENFORCEMENT;
    27→
    28→  if (explicit === 'throw') {
    29→    return isTestMode ? 'warn' : 'throw';
    30→  }
    31→  if (explicit === 'warn') {
    32→    return 'warn';
    33→  }
    34→
    35→  if (isTestMode) {
    36→    return 'warn';
    37→  }
    38→
    39→  return nodeEnv === 'production' ? 'warn' : 'throw';
    40→}
    41→
    42→/**
    43→ * Emits a one-time runtime signal when a legacy alias is used past its removal target.
    44→ * Returns true when the usage is past target, false otherwise.
    45→ */
    46→export function signalPastRemovalTargetUsage({
    47→  alias,
    48→  policy,
    49→  remediation,
    50→  enforcement = 'auto',
    51→}: DeprecationSignalOptions): boolean {
    52→  if (!isPastRemovalTarget(policy)) {
    53→    return false;
    54→  }
    55→
    56→  const key = `${alias}:${policy.removeBy}`;
    57→  if (signaledDeprecations.has(key)) {
    58→    return true;
    59→  }
    60→
    61→  signaledDeprecations.add(key);
    62→  const suffix = remediation ? ` ${remediation}` : '';
    63→  const message = `[deprecation] ${alias} is past removal target ${policy.removeBy} (owner: ${policy.owner}).${suffix}`;
    64→  const mode = resolveEnforcementMode(enforcement);
    65→  const logData = {
    66→    alias,
    67→    owner: policy.owner,
    68→    removeBy: policy.removeBy,
    69→    mode,
    70→  };
    71→
    72→  if (mode === 'throw') {
    73→    normalizeAndPresentAndRethrow(new Error(message), {
    74→      context: 'deprecationEnforcement.signalPastRemovalTargetUsage',
    75→      showToast: false,
    76→      logData,
    77→    });
    78→  }
    79→
    80→  normalizeAndPresentError(new Error(message), {
    81→    context: 'deprecationEnforcement.signalPastRemovalTargetUsage',
    82→    showToast: false,
    83→    logData,
    84→  });
    85→  return true;
    86→}

     2→ * Standardized error types for the application

     8→/**
     9→ * Base application error with additional context

    11→export class AppError extends Error {
    12→  /** Whether this error should be shown to the user via toast */
    13→  public readonly showToast: boolean;
    14→  /** Additional context for logging */
    15→  public readonly context?: Record<string, unknown>;
    16→  /** Original error if this wraps another error */

    18→

    24→      cause?: Error;
    25→    }
    26→  ) {
    27→    super(message);
    28→    this.name = 'AppError';
    29→    this.showToast = options?.showToast ?? true;
    30→    this.context = options?.context;
    31→    this.cause = options?.cause;
    32→  }
    33→}
    34→
    35→/**
    36→ * Network-related errors (fetch failures, timeouts, offline)
    37→ * These are often transient and may benefit from retry

    39→export class NetworkError extends AppError {
    40→  /** Whether the user appears to be offline */
    41→  public readonly isOffline: boolean;

    43→  public readonly isTimeout: boolean;
    44→
    45→  constructor(

    49→      isTimeout?: boolean;
    50→      context?: Record<string, unknown>;
    51→      cause?: Error;
    52→    }
    53→  ) {
    54→    super(message, { showToast: true, ...options });
    55→    this.name = 'NetworkError';
    56→    this.isOffline = options?.isOffline ?? !navigator.onLine;
    57→    this.isTimeout = options?.isTimeout ?? false;
    58→  }
    59→
    60→  static fromError(error: Error, context?: Record<string, unknown>): NetworkError {
    61→    const isTimeout = error.name === 'AbortError' || error.message.includes('timeout');
    62→    const isOffline = !navigator.onLine;
    63→
    64→    let message = 'Network request failed';
    65→    if (isOffline) {
    66→      message = 'You appear to be offline. Please check your connection.';
    67→    } else if (isTimeout) {
    68→      message = 'Request timed out. Please try again.';
    69→    }
    70→
    71→    return new NetworkError(message, { isOffline, isTimeout, context, cause: error });
    72→  }
    73→}

   153→ * Use for expected failures like localStorage unavailable, optional features

   155→export class SilentError extends AppError {

   157→    message: string,
   158→    options?: {
   159→      context?: Record<string, unknown>;

   161→    }

   169→ * Type guard to check if an error is one of our app errors
   170→ */
   171→export function isAppError(error: unknown): error is AppError {
   172→  return error instanceof AppError;

   176→ * Type guard to check if an error is a network error

   178→export function isNetworkError(error: unknown): error is NetworkError {

   189→/**
   190→ * Categorize an unknown error into an appropriate AppError type
   191→ */
   192→export function categorizeError(error: unknown, context?: Record<string, unknown>): AppError {
   193→  // Already an AppError
   194→  if (isAppError(error)) {
   195→    return error;
   196→  }
   197→
   198→  // Convert to Error if needed
   199→  const err = error instanceof Error ? error : new Error(String(error));
   200→  const message = err.message.toLowerCase();
   201→
   202→  // Network errors
   203→  if (
   204→    err.name === 'AbortError' ||
   205→    message.includes('network') ||
   206→    message.includes('fetch') ||
   207→    message.includes('timeout') ||
   208→    message.includes('failed to fetch') ||
   209→    !navigator.onLine
   210→  ) {
   211→    return NetworkError.fromError(err, context);
   212→  }
   213→
   214→  // Auth errors
   215→  if (
   216→    message.includes('unauthorized') ||
   217→    message.includes('forbidden') ||
   218→    message.includes('not authenticated') ||
   219→    message.includes('authentication required')
   220→  ) {
   221→    return AuthError.fromError(err, context);
   222→  }
   223→
   224→  // Validation errors
   225→  if (
   226→    message.includes('required') ||
   227→    message.includes('invalid') ||
   228→    message.includes('validation')
   229→  ) {
   230→    return new ValidationError(err.message, { context, cause: err });
   231→  }
   232→
   233→  // Default to generic AppError
   234→  return new AppError(err.message, { context, cause: err });
   235→}

     9→// Module-level request deduplication cache for the raw `users.settings` DB fetch.
    10→//
    11→// WHY THIS EXISTS (instead of React Query):
    12→// This hook reads a single key from `users.settings.ui`, but many instances
    13→// mount concurrently for different keys (generationMethods, privacyDefaults,
    14→// theme, etc.). Without deduplication, each mount fires an identical
    15→// `SELECT settings FROM users WHERE id = ?` query.
    16→//
    17→// WHY NOT React Query: The hook's read path has complex per-key logic
    18→// (fallback merging, normalization, auto-backfill of missing DB fields)
    19→// that runs after fetching the raw settings row. Migrating to React Query
    20→// would require either (a) a single shared query that all instances subscribe
    21→// to (losing per-key granularity for loading/error states), or (b) per-key
    22→// queries that each fetch the same row (defeating deduplication). The current
    23→// approach deduplicates at the network layer while keeping per-key logic local.
    24→//
    25→// WRITES already go through useToolSettings' global write queue, so there is
    26→// no write-side duplication -- only this read-side cache is parallel.
    27→interface CachedUserSettingsRow {
    28→  settings?: Json;
    29→}
    30→interface CachedSettingsResult {
    31→  data: CachedUserSettingsRow | null;
    32→  error: unknown;
    33→}
    34→interface SettingsCacheEntry {
    35→  data: CachedSettingsResult | null;
    36→  timestamp: number;
    37→  loading: Promise<CachedSettingsResult> | null;
    38→}
    39→const settingsCache = new Map<string, SettingsCacheEntry>();
    40→const CACHE_DURATION = 30000; // 30 seconds
    41→
    42→interface UISettings {
    43→  paneLocks: {
    44→    shots: boolean;
    45→    tasks: boolean;
    46→    gens: boolean;
    47→  };
    48→  settingsModal: {
    49→    activeTab: string;
    50→  };
    51→  videoTravelWidescreen: {
    52→    enabled: boolean;
    53→  };
    54→  imageDeletion?: {
    55→    skipConfirmation: boolean;
    56→  };
    57→  generationMethods: {
    58→    onComputer: boolean;
    59→    inCloud: boolean;
    60→  };
    61→  aiInputMode: {
    62→    mode: 'voice' | 'text';
    63→  };
    64→  privacyDefaults: {
    65→    resourcesPublic: boolean;
    66→    generationsPublic: boolean;
    67→  };
    68→  theme: {
    69→    darkMode: boolean; // Defaults to true (dark mode) for new users
    70→  };
    71→  productTour?: {
    72→    completed: boolean;
    73→    skipped: boolean;
    74→  };
    75→}
    76→
    77→function toRecord(value: unknown): Record<string, unknown> | undefined {
    78→  if (value && typeof value === 'object' && !Array.isArray(value)) {
    79→    return value as Record<string, unknown>;
    80→  }
    81→  return undefined;
    82→}
    83→
    84→// Cached settings loader to prevent duplicate database calls  
    85→const loadUserSettingsCached = async (userId: string) => {
    86→  const cacheKey = `user_settings_${userId}`;
    87→  const cached = settingsCache.get(cacheKey);
    88→  
    89→  // Return fresh cached data
    90→  if (cached && (Date.now() - cached.timestamp) < CACHE_DURATION) {
    91→    return cached.data;
    92→  }
    93→  
    94→  // If there's already a loading request, wait for it
    95→  if (cached?.loading) {
    96→    return await cached.loading;
    97→  }
    98→  
    99→  // Make new database call and cache the promise
   100→  const loadingPromise: Promise<CachedSettingsResult> = (async () => {
   101→    try {
   102→      const result = await supabase().from('users')
   103→        .select('settings')
   104→        .eq('id', userId)
   105→        .single();
   106→      const typedResult = result as unknown as CachedSettingsResult;
   107→      settingsCache.set(cacheKey, {
   108→        data: typedResult,
   109→        timestamp: Date.now(),
   110→        loading: null
   111→      });
   112→      return typedResult;
   113→    } catch (error) {
   114→      settingsCache.delete(cacheKey);
   115→      throw error;
   116→    }
   117→  })();
   118→  
   119→  // Cache the loading promise to prevent duplicate requests
   120→  settingsCache.set(cacheKey, {
   121→    data: cached?.data || null,
   122→    timestamp: cached?.timestamp || 0,
   123→    loading: loadingPromise
   124→  });
   125→  
   126→  return await loadingPromise;
   127→};
   128→
   129→/**
   130→ * Hook for user-scoped UI preferences (theme, pane locks, generation methods, etc.).
   131→ *
   132→ * Scope: user-only (stored in `users.settings.ui`).
   133→ * Auto-save: yes, 200ms debounce via the global settings write queue.
   134→ *
   135→ * Use this for preferences that follow the user across all projects/shots.
   136→ * For project/shot-scoped settings, use `useAutoSaveSettings` instead.
   137→ *
   138→ * @see docs/structure_detail/settings_system.md for the full settings hook decision tree
   139→ */
   140→export function useUserUIState<K extends keyof UISettings>(
   141→  key: K,
   142→  fallback: UISettings[K]
   143→) {
   144→  // Normalize logic specific to generationMethods to avoid ambiguous "both true" state.
   145→  // Allowed states:
   146→  // - inCloud: true, onComputer: false
   147→  // - inCloud: false, onComputer: true
   148→  // - inCloud: false, onComputer: false (explicitly disabled, used for warnings)
   149→  // Not allowed:
   150→  // - inCloud: true, onComputer: true → normalize to cloud by default
   151→  const normalizeIfGenerationMethods = useCallback((val: UISettings[K]): UISettings[K] => {
   152→    if ((key as string) !== 'generationMethods') return val;
   153→    if (!val || typeof val !== 'object') return val;
   154→    const valObj = val as unknown as Record<string, unknown>;
   155→    const inCloud = Boolean(valObj.inCloud);
   156→    const onComputer = Boolean(valObj.onComputer);
   157→    if (inCloud && onComputer) {
   158→      return { inCloud: true, onComputer: false } as UISettings[K];
   159→    }
   160→    return { inCloud, onComputer } as UISettings[K];
   161→  }, [key]);
   162→
   163→  // Stabilize fallback using a ref so callers can pass inline objects without causing
   164→  // infinite render loops. The load effect reads fallbackRef.current instead of depending
   165→  // on fallback directly, preventing re-runs when the reference changes but values don't.
   166→  const fallbackRef = useRef<UISettings[K]>(fallback);
   167→  fallbackRef.current = fallback;
   168→
   169→  useRenderLogger(`UserUIState:${key}`);
   170→
   171→  const [value, setValue] = useState<UISettings[K]>(fallback);
   172→  const [isLoading, setIsLoading] = useState(true);
   173→  const userIdRef = useRef<string>();
   174→  const debounceRef = useRef<NodeJS.Timeout>();
   175→  // Ref so that `update` can read the latest value without depending on it
   176→  const valueRef = useRef(value);
   177→  valueRef.current = value;
   178→
   179→  // Helper function to save fallback values to database (preserves all existing settings)
   180→  // This automatically backfills existing users with default values when they first load the app
   181→  // IMPORTANT: Only runs when the key is completely missing from database (undefined)
   182→  // Does NOT override explicit user choices (including both options set to false)
   183→  const saveFallbackToDatabase = useCallback(async (userId: string, _currentSettings: Record<string, unknown>) => {
   184→    try {
   185→      const fallbackToSave = normalizeIfGenerationMethods(fallbackRef.current);
   186→
   187→      // Use the global queue to save - it handles merging
   188→      await updateToolSettingsSupabase({
   189→        scope: 'user',
   190→        id: userId,
   191→        toolId: SETTINGS_IDS.USER_UI_STATE,
   192→        patch: { [key]: fallbackToSave },
   193→      }, 'immediate');
   194→
   195→      // Invalidate cache so other components see the backfilled values
   196→      const cacheKey = `user_settings_${userId}`;
   197→      settingsCache.delete(cacheKey);
   198→      setValue(fallbackToSave); // Update local state after successful save
   199→    } catch (error) {
   200→      normalizeAndPresentError(error, { context: 'useUserUIState.saveFallbackToDatabase', showToast: false });
   201→    }
   202→  }, [key, normalizeIfGenerationMethods]);
   203→
   204→  // Load initial value from database
   205→  useEffect(() => {
   206→    const loadUserSettings = async () => {
   207→      try {
   208→        const { data: { user } } = await supabase().auth.getUser();
   209→        if (!user) {
   210→          // Skip loading for unauthenticated users (e.g., on public share pages)
   211→          setIsLoading(false);
   212→          return;
   213→        }
   214→
   215→        userIdRef.current = user.id;
   216→
   217→        const cachedResult = await loadUserSettingsCached(user.id);
   218→        const data = cachedResult?.data ?? null;
   219→        const error = cachedResult?.error ?? null;
   220→
   221→        if (error) {
   222→          normalizeAndPresentError(error, { context: 'useUserUIState.loadSettings', showToast: false });
   223→          setIsLoading(false);
   224→          return;
   225→        }
   226→
   227→        const settingsRecord = toRecord(data?.settings);
   228→        const uiSettings = toRecord(settingsRecord?.ui);
   229→        const keyValue = uiSettings?.[key];
   230→        
   231→        if (keyValue !== undefined) {
   232→          // Key exists in database - merge with fallback to backfill any missing fields
   233→          const currentFallback = fallbackRef.current;
   234→          const mergedValue = (typeof currentFallback === 'object' && currentFallback !== null)
   235→            ? ({ ...currentFallback, ...(keyValue as object) } as UISettings[K])
   236→            : (keyValue as UISettings[K]);
   237→
   238→          const normalizedValue = normalizeIfGenerationMethods(mergedValue);
   239→          setValue(normalizedValue);
   240→
   241→          // If any fields from the fallback are missing in the stored value OR
   242→          // normalization changed the value, backfill them in DB
   243→          if (
   244→            (typeof keyValue === 'object' && keyValue !== null &&
   245→            typeof currentFallback === 'object' && currentFallback !== null &&
   246→            Object.keys(currentFallback as object).some((k) => (keyValue as Record<string, unknown>)[k] === undefined)) ||
   247→            JSON.stringify(normalizedValue) !== JSON.stringify(keyValue)
   248→          ) {
   249→            // Use the global queue to save - it handles merging
   250→            updateToolSettingsSupabase({
   251→              scope: 'user',
   252→              id: user.id,
   253→              toolId: SETTINGS_IDS.USER_UI_STATE,
   254→              patch: { [key]: normalizedValue },
   255→            }, 'immediate').then(() => {
   256→              const cacheKey = `user_settings_${user.id}`;
   257→              settingsCache.delete(cacheKey);
   258→            }).catch(e => {
   259→              normalizeAndPresentError(e, { context: 'useUserUIState.backfillFields', showToast: false });
   260→            });
   261→          }
   262→        } else {
   263→          // Key doesn't exist in database - this is an existing user who hasn't set preferences yet
   264→          // Save fallback values to backfill them (only runs when completely empty)
   265→          const normalizedFallback = normalizeIfGenerationMethods(fallbackRef.current);
   266→          setValue(normalizedFallback); // Set normalized fallback immediately for responsive UI
   267→
   268→          // Save to database in background (don't block loading)
   269→          saveFallbackToDatabase(user.id, settingsRecord || {}).catch(error => {
   270→            normalizeAndPresentError(error, { context: 'useUserUIState.saveFallback', showToast: false });
   271→          });
   272→        }
   273→
   274→        setIsLoading(false);
   275→      } catch (error) {
   276→        normalizeAndPresentError(error, { context: 'useUserUIState.loadUserSettings', showToast: false });
   277→        setIsLoading(false);
   278→      }
   279→    };
   280→
   281→    loadUserSettings();
   282→  }, [key, normalizeIfGenerationMethods, saveFallbackToDatabase]);
   283→
   284→  // Debounced update function
   285→  // Uses the global settings write queue (via updateToolSettingsSupabase) to prevent
   286→  // race conditions with other hooks that write to users.settings (e.g., useToolSettings
   287→  // writing user-preferences). The write queue serializes writes and uses an atomic RPC.
   288→  const update = useCallback((patch: Partial<UISettings[K]>) => {
   289→    // Immediately update local state for responsive UI (with normalization)
   290→    const normalizedPatch = normalizeIfGenerationMethods({
   291→      ...(valueRef.current as object),
   292→      ...(patch as object)
   293→    } as UISettings[K]);
   294→    setValue(normalizedPatch);
   295→
   296→    // Clear existing timeout
   297→    if (debounceRef.current) {
   298→      clearTimeout(debounceRef.current);
   299→    }
   300→
   301→    // Debounce the database write via the global settings write queue
   302→    debounceRef.current = setTimeout(async () => {
   303→      const userId = userIdRef.current;
   304→      if (!userId) return;
   305→
   306→      try {
   307→        // Use the write queue which handles atomic DB updates and merging.
   308→        // This prevents race conditions with other hooks writing to users.settings.
   309→        await updateToolSettingsSupabase({
   310→          scope: 'user',
   311→          id: userId,
   312→          toolId: SETTINGS_IDS.USER_UI_STATE,
   313→          patch: { [key]: normalizedPatch },
   314→        });
   315→
   316→        // Invalidate local cache so other useUserUIState instances see the update
   317→        const cacheKey = `user_settings_${userId}`;
   318→        settingsCache.delete(cacheKey);
   319→      } catch (error) {
   320→        normalizeAndPresentError(error, { context: 'useUserUIState.update', showToast: false });
   321→      }
   322→    }, 200);
   323→  }, [key, normalizeIfGenerationMethods]);
   324→
   325→  // Cleanup timeout on unmount
   326→  useEffect(() => {
   327→    return () => {
   328→      if (debounceRef.current) {
   329→        clearTimeout(debounceRef.current);
   330→      }
   331→    };
   332→  }, []);
   333→
   334→  return useMemo(() => ({
   335→    value,
   336→    update,
   337→    isLoading
   338→  }), [value, update, isLoading]);
   339→} 
   340→

    44→
    45→---
    46→
    47→## Tech Stack
    48→
    49→| Layer | Technology | Purpose |
    50→|-------|------------|---------|
    51→| **Frontend** | React + Vite + TypeScript | SPA framework & build tooling |
    52→| **Styling** | TailwindCSS + shadcn-ui | Utility CSS with container queries (`@container`) |
    53→| **Backend** | Supabase (Postgres + Edge Functions) | Database, auth, storage, serverless workers |
    54→
    55→**Dev server:** `http://localhost:2222` • **Package managers:** npm (default) or bun
    56→
    57→---
    58→
    59→## Directory Structure
    60→
    61→| Path | Purpose | Key Files |
    62→|------|---------|-----------|
    63→| `/src/app` | App bootstrap & routing | `main.tsx` → `App.tsx` → `routes.tsx` → `Layout.tsx` |
    64→| `/src/pages` | Top-level pages | `HomePage`, `ShotsPage`, `ArtPage`, `SharePage`, `NotFoundPage`, payment pages |
    65→| `/src/tools` | Feature modules | Each tool: `pages/`, `components/`, `hooks/`, `settings.ts` |
    66→| `/src/shared` | Shared code | `components/ui/` (shadcn), `hooks/`, `contexts/`, `lib/` |
    67→| `/supabase/functions` | Edge Functions | Task processing, payments, AI integration |
    68→| `/supabase/migrations` | DB migrations | Schema changes (use `db push --linked`) |
    69→| Root | Build configs | `vite.config.ts`, `tailwind.config.ts`, `railway.toml` |
    70→
    71→---
    72→
    73→## Core Concepts
    74→
    75→### Tools
    76→Tools live in `/src/tools/{tool-name}/` following a consistent structure. See [adding_new_tool.md](docs/structure_detail/adding_new_tool.md).
    77→
    78→**Active tools:** Image Generation, Video Travel, Animate Characters, Edit Images, Edit Video, Join Clips, Training Data Helper
    79→
    80→### Shots & Generations
    81→- **Generations** = gallery items (images/videos produced by AI tasks)
    82→- **Shots** = containers that organize generations into a timeline
    83→- **`shot_generations`** = join table with position + metadata (pair prompts, timeline frame)
    84→- Data access: `useShotImages(shotId)` → see [data_fetching.md](docs/structure_detail/data_fetching.md)
    85→
    86→### Settings Resolution
    87→Priority: **shot → project → user → defaults**. See [settings_system.md](docs/structure_detail/settings_system.md).
    88→
    89→### Task System
    90→Async queue for AI workloads: client creates task → DB trigger → worker polls → Edge Function completes.
    91→See [task_worker_lifecycle.md](docs/structure_detail/task_worker_lifecycle.md).
    92→
    93→### Realtime
    94→Smart polling + Supabase realtime subscriptions. Connected = no polling; disconnected = 15s fallback.
    95→See [realtime_system.md](docs/structure_detail/realtime_system.md).
    96→
    97→---
    98→
    99→## Key Utilities
   100→
   101→| System | Location | Purpose |
   102→|--------|----------|---------|
   103→| **queryKeys** | `lib/queryKeys.ts` | Central registry for all React Query cache keys |
   104→| **errors** | `lib/errors.ts` | Typed error classes (`NetworkError`, `AuthError`, `ValidationError`, etc.) |
   105→| **errorHandler** | `lib/errorHandler.ts` | Centralized `handleError()` with logging + toast |
   106→| **AppErrorBoundary** | `components/AppErrorBoundary.tsx` | App-level crash recovery UI |
   107→| **ModalContainer** | `components/ModalContainer.tsx` | Unified responsive modal with header/footer/scroll |
   108→| **ConfirmDialog** | `components/ConfirmDialog.tsx` | Promise-based confirmation dialogs with presets |
   109→| **settingsResolution** | `lib/settingsResolution.ts` | Resolve settings across scopes |
   110→| **settingsWriteQueue** | `lib/settingsWriteQueue.ts` | Global queue for settings writes (prevents network flooding) |
   111→| **debugConfig** | `lib/debugConfig.ts` | Runtime debug logging (`window.debugConfig`) |
   112→| **taskConfig** | `lib/taskConfig.ts` | Task visibility & display names |
   113→| **performanceUtils** | `lib/performanceUtils.ts` | Frame budget monitoring |
   114→
   115→Instrumentation lives in `src/integrations/supabase/instrumentation/` — see its [README](src/integrations/supabase/instrumentation/README.md).
   116→
   117→---
   118→
   119→## Development
   120→
   121→See [README.md](README.md) for local setup, commands, mobile testing, and troubleshooting.
   122→
   123→**Debug logging:** `VITE_DEBUG_LOGS=true npm run dev` — see [debugging.md](docs/structure_detail/debugging.md)

    44→
    45→---
    46→
    47→## Tech Stack
    48→
    49→| Layer | Technology | Purpose |
    50→|-------|------------|---------|
    51→| **Frontend** | React + Vite + TypeScript | SPA framework & build tooling |
    52→| **Styling** | TailwindCSS + shadcn-ui | Utility CSS with container queries (`@container`) |
    53→| **Backend** | Supabase (Postgres + Edge Functions) | Database, auth, storage, serverless workers |
    54→
    55→**Dev server:** `http://localhost:2222` • **Package managers:** npm (default) or bun
    56→
    57→---
    58→
    59→## Directory Structure
    60→
    61→| Path | Purpose | Key Files |
    62→|------|---------|-----------|
    63→| `/src/app` | App bootstrap & routing | `main.tsx` → `App.tsx` → `routes.tsx` → `Layout.tsx` |
    64→| `/src/pages` | Top-level pages | `HomePage`, `ShotsPage`, `ArtPage`, `SharePage`, `NotFoundPage`, payment pages |
    65→| `/src/tools` | Feature modules | Each tool: `pages/`, `components/`, `hooks/`, `settings.ts` |
    66→| `/src/shared` | Shared code | `components/ui/` (shadcn), `hooks/`, `contexts/`, `lib/` |
    67→| `/supabase/functions` | Edge Functions | Task processing, payments, AI integration |
    68→| `/supabase/migrations` | DB migrations | Schema changes (use `db push --linked`) |
    69→| Root | Build configs | `vite.config.ts`, `tailwind.config.ts`, `railway.toml` |
    70→
    71→---
    72→
    73→## Core Concepts
    74→
    75→### Tools
    76→Tools live in `/src/tools/{tool-name}/` following a consistent structure. See [adding_new_tool.md](docs/structure_detail/adding_new_tool.md).
    77→
    78→**Active tools:** Image Generation, Video Travel, Animate Characters, Edit Images, Edit Video, Join Clips, Training Data Helper
    79→
    80→### Shots & Generations
    81→- **Generations** = gallery items (images/videos produced by AI tasks)
    82→- **Shots** = containers that organize generations into a timeline
    83→- **`shot_generations`** = join table with position + metadata (pair prompts, timeline frame)
    84→- Data access: `useShotImages(shotId)` → see [data_fetching.md](docs/structure_detail/data_fetching.md)
    85→
    86→### Settings Resolution
    87→Priority: **shot → project → user → defaults**. See [settings_system.md](docs/structure_detail/settings_system.md).
    88→
    89→### Task System
    90→Async queue for AI workloads: client creates task → DB trigger → worker polls → Edge Function completes.
    91→See [task_worker_lifecycle.md](docs/structure_detail/task_worker_lifecycle.md).
    92→
    93→### Realtime
    94→Smart polling + Supabase realtime subscriptions. Connected = no polling; disconnected = 15s fallback.
    95→See [realtime_system.md](docs/structure_detail/realtime_system.md).
    96→
    97→---
    98→
    99→## Key Utilities
   100→
   101→| System | Location | Purpose |
   102→|--------|----------|---------|
   103→| **queryKeys** | `lib/queryKeys.ts` | Central registry for all React Query cache keys |
   104→| **errors** | `lib/errors.ts` | Typed error classes (`NetworkError`, `AuthError`, `ValidationError`, etc.) |
   105→| **errorHandler** | `lib/errorHandler.ts` | Centralized `handleError()` with logging + toast |
   106→| **AppErrorBoundary** | `components/AppErrorBoundary.tsx` | App-level crash recovery UI |
   107→| **ModalContainer** | `components/ModalContainer.tsx` | Unified responsive modal with header/footer/scroll |
   108→| **ConfirmDialog** | `components/ConfirmDialog.tsx` | Promise-based confirmation dialogs with presets |
   109→| **settingsResolution** | `lib/settingsResolution.ts` | Resolve settings across scopes |
   110→| **settingsWriteQueue** | `lib/settingsWriteQueue.ts` | Global queue for settings writes (prevents network flooding) |
   111→| **debugConfig** | `lib/debugConfig.ts` | Runtime debug logging (`window.debugConfig`) |
   112→| **taskConfig** | `lib/taskConfig.ts` | Task visibility & display names |
   113→| **performanceUtils** | `lib/performanceUtils.ts` | Frame budget monitoring |
   114→
   115→Instrumentation lives in `src/integrations/supabase/instrumentation/` — see its [README](src/integrations/supabase/instrumentation/README.md).
   116→
   117→---
   118→
   119→## Development
   120→
   121→See [README.md](README.md) for local setup, commands, mobile testing, and troubleshooting.
   122→
   123→**Debug logging:** `VITE_DEBUG_LOGS=true npm run dev` — see [debugging.md](docs/structure_detail/debugging.md)

    81→- **Generations** = gallery items (images/videos produced by AI tasks)
    82→- **Shots** = containers that organize generations into a timeline

    87→Priority: **shot → project → user → defaults**. See [settings_system.md](docs/structure_detail/settings_system.md).
    88→
    89→### Task System
    90→Async queue for AI workloads: client creates task → DB trigger → worker polls → Edge Function completes.
    91→See [task_worker_lifecycle.md](docs/structure_detail/task_worker_lifecycle.md).
    92→
    93→### Realtime
    94→Smart polling + Supabase realtime subscriptions. Connected = no polling; disconnected = 15s fallback.
    95→See [realtime_system.md](docs/structure_detail/realtime_system.md).

1→/**
     2→ * Global Settings Write Queue
     3→ *
     4→ * Prevents network exhaustion by serializing and coalescing settings writes.
     5→ *
     6→ * Features:
     7→ * - Global concurrency limit (default: 1 in-flight write)
     8→ * - Per-target debouncing (coalesces rapid updates)
     9→ * - Merge-on-write (latest patch wins per field)
    10→ * - Optional AbortSignal passthrough for caller cancellation
    11→ * - Best-effort flush on page unload
    12→ *
    13→ * @see settings_system.md for the full settings architecture
    14→ */
    15→
    16→import { normalizeAndPresentError } from '@/shared/lib/errorHandling/runtimeError';
    17→
    18→export interface QueuedWrite {
    19→  scope: 'user' | 'project' | 'shot';
    20→  entityId: string;
    21→  toolId: string;
    22→  patch: Record<string, unknown>;
    23→  signal?: AbortSignal;
    24→}
    25→
    26→interface PendingWrite {
    27→  write: QueuedWrite;
    28→  resolvers: Array<{ resolve: (value: unknown) => void; reject: (error: unknown) => void }>;
    29→  timerId: NodeJS.Timeout | null;
    30→  enqueuedAt: number;
    31→}
    32→
    33→// Configuration
    34→const DEBOUNCE_MS = 300;
    35→const MAX_CONCURRENT = 1;
    36→
    37→// State
    38→const pendingByTarget = new Map<string, PendingWrite>();
    39→let inFlightCount = 0;
    40→const flushQueue: Array<{ targetKey: string; pending: PendingWrite }> = [];
    41→
    42→// The actual write function - injected to avoid circular imports
    43→let writeFunction: ((write: QueuedWrite) => Promise<unknown>) | null = null;
    44→
    45→function createAbortError(): Error {
    46→  if (typeof DOMException !== 'undefined') {
    47→    return new DOMException('Request was cancelled', 'AbortError');
    48→  }
    49→  const error = new Error('Request was cancelled');
    50→  error.name = 'AbortError';
    51→  return error;
    52→}
    53→
    54→function throwIfAborted(signal?: AbortSignal): void {
    55→  if (signal?.aborted) {
    56→    throw createAbortError();
    57→  }
    58→}
    59→
    60→/**
    61→ * Set the write function that performs the actual DB update.
    62→ * Must be called once at app init (in useToolSettings.ts).
    63→ * Also registers page-unload listeners on first call (deferred from module load).
    64→ */
    65→export function setSettingsWriteFunction(fn: (write: QueuedWrite) => Promise<unknown>) {
    66→  const isFirstInit = writeFunction === null;
    67→  writeFunction = fn;
    68→
    69→  if (isFirstInit && typeof window !== 'undefined') {
    70→    window.addEventListener('beforeunload', () => {
    71→      flushAll();
    72→    });
    73→    document.addEventListener('visibilitychange', () => {
    74→      if (document.visibilityState === 'hidden') {
    75→        flushAll();
    76→      }
    77→    });
    78→  }
    79→}
    80→
    81→/**
    82→ * Create a unique key for deduplication
    83→ */
    84→function targetKey(write: QueuedWrite): string {
    85→  return `${write.scope}:${write.entityId}:${write.toolId}`;
    86→}
    87→
    88→/**
    89→ * Shallow merge (one level deep)
    90→ */
    91→function shallowMergePatch(existing: Record<string, unknown>, incoming: Record<string, unknown>): Record<string, unknown> {
    92→  return { ...existing, ...incoming };
    93→}
    94→
    95→/**
    96→ * Process the next item in the flush queue
    97→ */
    98→async function processQueue() {
    99→  if (inFlightCount >= MAX_CONCURRENT || flushQueue.length === 0) {
   100→    return;
   101→  }
   102→
   103→  const next = flushQueue.shift();
   104→  if (!next) return;
   105→
   106→  const { targetKey: key, pending } = next;
   107→  
   108→  // Remove from pending map (we're about to process it)
   109→  pendingByTarget.delete(key);
   110→  
   111→  inFlightCount++;
   112→  
   113→  try {
   114→    if (!writeFunction) {
   115→      throw new Error('[SettingsWriteQueue] Write function not initialized');
   116→    }
   117→
   118→    throwIfAborted(pending.write.signal);
   119→    const result = await writeFunction(pending.write);
   120→    
   121→    // Resolve all waiters
   122→    for (const { resolve } of pending.resolvers) {
   123→      resolve(result);
   124→    }
   125→  } catch (error) {
   126→    normalizeAndPresentError(error, { context: 'SettingsWriteQueue', showToast: false });
   127→
   128→    // Reject all waiters
   129→    for (const { reject } of pending.resolvers) {
   130→      reject(error);
   131→    }
   132→  } finally {
   133→    inFlightCount--;
   134→    
   135→    // Process next item
   136→    processQueue();
   137→  }
   138→}
   139→
   140→/**
   141→ * Schedule a pending write for flush
   142→ */
   143→function scheduleFlush(key: string, pending: PendingWrite) {
   144→  // Clear existing timer
   145→  if (pending.timerId) {
   146→    clearTimeout(pending.timerId);
   147→    pending.timerId = null;
   148→  }
   149→  
   150→  // Add to flush queue and process
   151→  flushQueue.push({ targetKey: key, pending });
   152→  processQueue();
   153→}
   154→
   155→/**
   156→ * Enqueue a settings write.
   157→ * 
   158→ * Returns a promise that resolves when the write completes.
   159→ * Multiple writes to the same target within the debounce window are merged.
   160→ * 
   161→ * @param write - The write to enqueue
   162→ * @param mode - 'debounced' (default) waits for debounce window; 'immediate' flushes now
   163→ */
   164→export function enqueueSettingsWrite(
   165→  write: QueuedWrite,
   166→  mode: 'debounced' | 'immediate' = 'debounced'
   167→): Promise<unknown> {
   168→  const key = targetKey(write);
   169→
   170→  return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
   171→    if (write.signal?.aborted) {
   172→      reject(createAbortError());
   173→      return;
   174→    }
   175→
   176→    const existing = pendingByTarget.get(key);
   177→
   178→    if (existing) {
   179→      // Merge with existing pending write
   180→      existing.write.patch = shallowMergePatch(existing.write.patch, write.patch);
   181→      if (write.signal) {
   182→        existing.write.signal = write.signal;
   183→      }
   184→      existing.resolvers.push({ resolve, reject });
   185→
   186→      if (mode === 'immediate') {
   187→        // Cancel debounce timer and flush now
   188→        scheduleFlush(key, existing);
   189→      }
   190→      // else: existing timer will handle it
   191→      
   192→    } else {
   193→      // Create new pending write
   194→      const pending: PendingWrite = {
   195→        write: { ...write, patch: { ...write.patch } },
   196→        resolvers: [{ resolve, reject }],
   197→        timerId: null,
   198→        enqueuedAt: Date.now(),
   199→      };
   200→
   201→      pendingByTarget.set(key, pending);
   202→
   203→      if (mode === 'immediate') {
   204→        scheduleFlush(key, pending);
   205→      } else {
   206→        // Set debounce timer
   207→        pending.timerId = setTimeout(() => {
   208→          scheduleFlush(key, pending);
   209→        }, DEBOUNCE_MS);
   210→      }
   211→    }
   212→  });
   213→}
   214→
   215→
   216→/**
   217→ * Flush all pending writes immediately.
   218→ * Best-effort: returns without waiting.
   219→ */
   220→function flushAll(): void {
   221→  for (const [key, pending] of pendingByTarget.entries()) {
   222→    if (pending.timerId) {
   223→      clearTimeout(pending.timerId);
   224→      pending.timerId = null;
   225→    }
   226→    flushQueue.push({ targetKey: key, pending });
   227→  }
   228→  pendingByTarget.clear();
   229→  processQueue();
   230→}
   231→
   232→

   218→            const isPublic = 'is_public' in metadata ? Boolean((metadata as Record<string, unknown>).is_public) : false;
   219→            
   220→            const { data, error } = await supabase().from('resources')
   221→                    .insert({
   222→                        type,
   223→                        metadata: toJson(metadata),
   224→                        user_id: user.id,
   225→                        is_public: isPublic
   226→                    })
   227→                .select()

   232→        },
   233→        onSuccess: (data) => {
   234→            queryClient.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: [...resourceQueryKeys.all, data.type] });
   235→            queryClient.invalidateQueries({ [REDACTED](data.type) });
   236→        },
   237→        onError: (error) => {
   238→            normalizeAndPresentError(error, { context: 'useCreateResource', toastTitle: 'Failed to create resource' });
   239→        },
   240→    });
   241→};
   242→
   243→// Update a resource
   244→export interface UpdateResourceArgs {
   245→    id: string;
   246→    type: ResourceType;
   247→    metadata: ResourceMetadata;
   248→}
   249→
   250→export const useUpdateResource = () => {
   251→    const queryClient = useQueryClient();
   252→    return useMutation<Resource, Error, UpdateResourceArgs>({
   253→        mutationFn: async ({ id, metadata }) => {
   254→
   255→            const { data: { user } } = await supabase().auth.getUser();
   256→            if (!user) {
   257→                const err = new Error('Not authenticated');
   258→                normalizeAndPresentError(err, { context: 'useUpdateResource', showToast: false });
   259→                throw err;
   260→            }
   261→
   262→            // First, let's check if the resource exists at all (without user_id filter)
   263→            const { data: resourceCheck } = await supabase().from('resources')
   264→                .select('id, user_id, type')
   265→                .eq('id', id)
   266→                .maybeSingle();
   267→            
   268→            // Now verify the resource exists and belongs to the user
   269→            const { data: existingResource, error: checkError } = await supabase().from('resources')
   270→                .select('id, user_id, type')
   271→                .eq('id', id)
   272→                .eq('user_id', user.id)
   273→                .maybeSingle();
   274→            
   275→            if (checkError) {
   276→                normalizeAndPresentError(checkError, { context: 'useUpdateResource', showToast: false });
   277→                throw new Error(`Failed to verify resource: ${checkError.message}`);
   278→            }
   279→            
   280→            if (!existingResource) {
   281→                normalizeAndPresentError(new Error('Resource not found or access denied'), { context: 'useUpdateResource', showToast: false, logData: {
   282→                    id,
   283→                    userId: user.id,
   284→                    resourceExists: !!resourceCheck,
   285→                    resourceOwner: resourceCheck?.user_id
   286→                }});
   287→
   288→                // Provide a more specific error message
   289→                if (resourceCheck && resourceCheck.user_id !== user.id) {
   290→                    throw new Error('This resource belongs to another user');
   291→                }
   292→                throw new Error('Resource not found or you do not have permission to update it');
   293→            }
   294→            
   295→            // Extract is_public from metadata for the column
   296→            const isPublic = 'is_public' in metadata ? Boolean((metadata as Record<string, unknown>).is_public) : false;
   297→            
   298→            // Now perform the update
   299→            const { data, error } = await supabase().from('resources')
   300→                .update({ metadata: toJson(metadata), is_public: isPublic })
   301→                .eq('id', id)
   302→                .eq('user_id', user.id)
   303→                .select()
   304→                .maybeSingle();
   305→            
   306→            if (error) {
   307→                normalizeAndPresentError(error, { context: 'useUpdateResource', showToast: false, logData: {
   308→                    code: error.code,
   309→                    details: error.details,
   310→                    hint: error.hint
   311→                }});
   312→                throw error;
   313→            }
   314→            
   315→            if (!data) {
   316→                normalizeAndPresentError(new Error('Update succeeded but no data returned'), { context: 'useUpdateResource', showToast: false });
   317→                // If update succeeded but no data returned, fetch it separately
   318→                const { data: fetchedData, error: fetchError } = await supabase().from('resources')
   319→                    .select('*')
   320→                    .eq('id', id)
   321→                    .maybeSingle();
   322→                
   323→                if (fetchError || !fetchedData) {
   324→                    normalizeAndPresentError(fetchError || new Error('No data returned'), { context: 'useUpdateResource', showToast: false });
   325→                    throw new Error('Update may have succeeded but failed to fetch updated resource');
   326→                }
   327→                
   328→                return mapResourceRow(fetchedData, existingResource.type as ResourceType);
   329→            }
   330→            
   331→            return mapResourceRow(data, existingResource.type as ResourceType);
   332→        },
   333→        onSuccess: (data) => {
   334→            // Prefix invalidation: ['resources', type] prefix-matches ['resources', type, 'v2']
   335→            queryClient.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: [...resourceQueryKeys.all, data.type] });
   336→            queryClient.invalidateQueries({ [REDACTED](data.type) });
   337→            // Invalidate specific-resources queries that include this resource ID
   338→            // Using predicate to find any query that contains this resource ID
   339→            queryClient.invalidateQueries({
   340→                predicate: (query) => {
   341→                    const key = query.queryKey;
   342→                    if (key[0] === 'specific-resources' && typeof key[1] === 'string') {
   343→                        return key[1].includes(data.id);
   344→                    }
   345→                    return false;
   346→                }
   347→            });
   348→        },
   349→        onError: (error) => {
   350→            normalizeAndPresentError(error, { context: 'useUpdateResource', toastTitle: 'Failed to update resource' });
   351→        },
   352→    });
   353→};
   354→
   355→// Delete a resource
   356→export const useDeleteResource = () => {
   357→    const queryClient = useQueryClient();
   358→    return useMutation<void, Error, { id: string, type: ResourceType }>({
   359→        mutationFn: async ({ id }) => {
   360→            const { data: { user } } = await supabase().auth.getUser();
   361→            if (!user) throw new Error('Not authenticated');
   362→
   363→            const { error } = await supabase().from('resources')
   364→                .delete()
   365→                .eq('id', id)
   366→                .eq('user_id', user.id);
   367→
   368→            if (error) throw error;
   369→        },
   370→        onSuccess: (_data, variables) => {
   371→            // Remove the individual resource cache entry
   372→            queryClient.removeQueries({ [REDACTED](variables.id) });
   373→            // Also invalidate the list queries
   374→            queryClient.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: [...resourceQueryKeys.all, variables.type] });
   375→            queryClient.invalidateQueries({ [REDACTED](variables.type) });
   376→        },
   377→        onError: (error) => {
   378→            normalizeAndPresentError(error, { context: 'useDeleteResource', toastTitle: 'Failed to delete resource' });
   379→        },
   380→    });
   381→};
   382→

1→/**
     2→ * usePendingGenerationTasks Hook
     3→ *
     4→ * Tracks tasks that are "Queued" or "In Progress" that will create
     5→ * variants or derived generations from a given source generation.
     6→ *
     7→ * Works for both images and videos - checks task params for source generation references.
     8→ */
     9→
    10→import { useMemo } from 'react';
    11→import { useQuery } from '@tanstack/react-query';
    12→import { getSupabaseClient as supabase } from '@/integrations/supabase/client';
    13→import { TASK_STATUS } from '@/types/tasks';
    14→import { taskQueryKeys } from '@/shared/lib/queryKeys/tasks';
    15→
    16→interface PendingGenerationTask {
    17→  id: string;
    18→  status: string;
    19→  task_type: string;
    20→}
    21→
    22→interface UsePendingGenerationTasksReturn {
    23→  /** Number of pending tasks that will create variants/derived from this generation */
    24→  pendingCount: number;
    25→  /** The pending tasks */
    26→  pendingTasks: PendingGenerationTask[];
    27→  /** Loading state */
    28→  isLoading: boolean;
    29→}
    30→
    31→/**
    32→ * Check if task params reference a specific generation ID as a source.
    33→ * Checks common param fields where source generation is stored.
    34→ */
    35→function taskReferencesGeneration(params: Record<string, unknown> | null, generationId: string): boolean {
    36→  if (!params || !generationId) return false;
    37→
    38→  // Direct source references
    39→  if (params.based_on === generationId) return true;
    40→  if (params.source_generation_id === generationId) return true;
    41→  if (params.generation_id === generationId) return true;
    42→  if (params.input_generation_id === generationId) return true;
    43→  if (params.parent_generation_id === generationId) return true;
    44→  // Video segment tasks use pair_shot_generation_id
    45→  if (params.pair_shot_generation_id === generationId) return true;
    46→
    47→  // Check nested in orchestrator_details
    48→  const orchDetails = params.orchestrator_details as Record<string, unknown> | undefined;
    49→  if (orchDetails) {
    50→    if (orchDetails.based_on === generationId) return true;
    51→    if (orchDetails.source_generation_id === generationId) return true;
    52→    if (orchDetails.parent_generation_id === generationId) return true;
    53→    // Check pair_shot_generation_ids array
    54→    if (Array.isArray(orchDetails.pair_shot_generation_ids)) {
    55→      if (orchDetails.pair_shot_generation_ids.includes(generationId)) return true;
    56→    }
    57→  }
    58→
    59→  // Check full_orchestrator_payload
    60→  const fullPayload = params.full_orchestrator_payload as Record<string, unknown> | undefined;
    61→  if (fullPayload) {
    62→    if (fullPayload.based_on === generationId) return true;
    63→    if (fullPayload.source_generation_id === generationId) return true;
    64→    if (fullPayload.parent_generation_id === generationId) return true;
    65→  }
    66→
    67→  // Check individual_segment_params (used by individual_travel_segment)
    68→  const individualParams = params.individual_segment_params as Record<string, unknown> | undefined;
    69→  if (individualParams) {
    70→    if (individualParams.pair_shot_generation_id === generationId) return true;
    71→  }
    72→
    73→  return false;
    74→}
    75→
    76→export function usePendingGenerationTasks(
    77→  generationId: string | null | undefined,
    78→  projectId: string | null | undefined
    79→): UsePendingGenerationTasksReturn {
    80→  // Query pending tasks for this project
    81→  const { data: pendingTasks, isLoading } = useQuery({
    82→    queryKey: [...taskQueryKeys.pendingGeneration(generationId!), projectId],
    83→    queryFn: async () => {
    84→      if (!generationId || !projectId) return [];
    85→
    86→      // Query tasks that are Queued or In Progress
    87→      const { data, error } = await supabase().from('tasks')
    88→        .select('id, status, task_type, params')
    89→        .eq('project_id', projectId)
    90→        .in('status', [TASK_STATUS.QUEUED, TASK_STATUS.IN_PROGRESS]);
    91→
    92→      if (error) {
    93→        console.error('[usePendingGenerationTasks] Query error:', error);
    94→        return [];
    95→      }
    96→
    97→      // Filter to tasks that reference this generation
    98→      const matchingTasks: PendingGenerationTask[] = (data || [])
    99→        .filter(task => taskReferencesGeneration(task.params as Record<string, unknown> | null, generationId))
   100→        .map(task => ({
   101→          id: task.id,
   102→          status: task.status,
   103→          task_type: task.task_type,
   104→        }));
   105→
   106→      return matchingTasks;
   107→    },
   108→    enabled: !!generationId && !!projectId,
   109→    // Poll to catch status changes
   110→    refetchInterval: 5000,
   111→    // Mark as stale immediately so invalidations trigger refetch
   112→    staleTime: 0,
   113→    // Short cache time - don't keep stale data around
   114→    gcTime: 10000,
   115→    // Always refetch when window regains focus
   116→    refetchOnWindowFocus: 'always',
   117→  });
   118→
   119→  const result = useMemo(() => ({
   120→    pendingCount: pendingTasks?.length || 0,
   121→    pendingTasks: pendingTasks || [],
   122→    isLoading,
   123→  }), [pendingTasks, isLoading]);
   124→
   125→  return result;
   126→}
   127→
   128→// NOTE: Default export removed - use named export { usePendingGenerationTasks } instead
   129→

    51→  const candidate = query as T & AbortSignalCapable<T>;
    52→  if (typeof candidate.abortSignal === 'function') {
    53→    return candidate.abortSignal(signal);
    54→  }
    55→
    56→  return query;
    57→}
    58→
    59→function throwIfAborted(signal?: AbortSignal): void {
    60→  if (signal?.aborted) {
    61→    throw new ToolSettingsError('cancelled', 'Request was cancelled', {
    62→      recoverable: true,
    63→      cause: signal.reason,
    64→    });
    65→  }
    66→}
    67→
    68→/**
    69→ * Raw write function - performs the actual DB update.
    70→ * Used internally by the settings write queue.
    71→ *
    72→ * @internal Use updateToolSettingsSupabase (queued) for normal usage
    73→ */
    74→async function fetchSettingsForScope(
    75→  scope: SettingsScope,
    76→  id: string,
    77→  signal?: AbortSignal,
    78→) {
    79→  throwIfAborted(signal);
    80→
    81→  return maybeAttachAbortSignal(selectSettingsForScope(scope, id), signal);
    82→}
    83→
    84→async function rawUpdateToolSettings(write: QueuedWrite): Promise<Record<string, unknown>> {
    85→  const { scope, entityId: id, toolId, patch, signal } = write;
    86→
    87→  try {
    88→    if (scope !== 'user' && scope !== 'project' && scope !== 'shot') {
    89→      throw new ToolSettingsError(
    90→        'invalid_scope_identifier',
    91→        `Invalid scope: ${scope}`,
    92→      );
    93→    }
    94→
    95→    const tableName = resolveSettingsScopeTable(scope);
    96→
    97→    // For patch updates, we need to fetch current settings to merge
    98→    // This is necessary because the caller provides a partial update
    99→    // TODO: In the future, consider passing full settings to eliminate this fetch
   100→    const { data: currentEntity, error: fetchError } = await fetchSettingsForScope(scope, id, signal);

    24→  const stableShotId = React.useMemo(() => shotId, [shotId]);

    43→    // refetchOnMount: 'always' ensures fresh data when opening a shot without the loop.

     8→export interface RuntimeErrorOptions extends ErrorReportOptions {
     9→  toastTitle?: string;

    12→
    13→/** Normalize unknown errors and route them through the shared presenter. */
    14→export function normalizeAndPresentError(error: unknown, options: RuntimeErrorOptions): AppError {
    15→  const { context, logData, onError, toastTitle, showToast } = options;
    16→  const appError = reportError(error, { context, logData, onError });
    17→
    18→  const shouldShowToast = showToast ?? appError.showToast;
    19→  if (shouldShowToast) {
    20→    presentRuntimeError(appError, toastTitle);
    21→  }
    22→
    23→  return appError;
    24→}

    27→export function normalizeAndPresentAndRethrow(error: unknown, options: RuntimeErrorOptions): never {

    11→export class AppError extends Error {

   147→    this.statusCode = options?.statusCode;
   148→  }
   149→}
   150→
   151→/**
   152→ * Errors that should be silently logged (not shown to user)
   153→ * Use for expected failures like localStorage unavailable, optional features
   154→ */
   155→export class SilentError extends AppError {
   156→  constructor(
   157→    message: string,
   158→    options?: {
   159→      context?: Record<string, unknown>;
   160→      cause?: Error;
   161→    }
   162→  ) {
   163→    super(message, { showToast: false, ...options });
   164→    this.name = 'SilentError';
   165→  }
   166→}
   167→
   168→/**
   169→ * Type guard to check if an error is one of our app errors
   170→ */
   171→export function isAppError(error: unknown): error is AppError {
   172→  return error instanceof AppError;
   173→}
   174→
   175→/**
   176→ * Type guard to check if an error is a network error
   177→ */
   178→export function isNetworkError(error: unknown): error is NetworkError {
   179→  return error instanceof NetworkError;
   180→}
   181→
   182→/**
   183→ * Type guard to check if an error is an auth error
   184→ */
   185→export function isAuthError(error: unknown): error is AuthError {
   186→  return error instanceof AuthError;
   187→}
   188→
   189→/**
   190→ * Categorize an unknown error into an appropriate AppError type
   191→ */
   192→export function categorizeError(error: unknown, context?: Record<string, unknown>): AppError {
   193→  // Already an AppError
   194→  if (isAppError(error)) {
   195→    return error;
   196→  }
   197→
   198→  // Convert to Error if needed
   199→  const err = error instanceof Error ? error : new Error(String(error));
   200→  const message = err.message.toLowerCase();
   201→
   202→  // Network errors
   203→  if (
   204→    err.name === 'AbortError' ||
   205→    message.includes('network') ||
   206→    message.includes('fetch') ||
   207→    message.includes('timeout') ||
   208→    message.includes('failed to fetch') ||
   209→    !navigator.onLine
   210→  ) {
   211→    return NetworkError.fromError(err, context);
   212→  }
   213→
   214→  // Auth errors
   215→  if (
   216→    message.includes('unauthorized') ||
   217→    message.includes('forbidden') ||
   218→    message.includes('not authenticated') ||
   219→    message.includes('authentication required')
   220→  ) {
   221→    return AuthError.fromError(err, context);
   222→  }
   223→
   224→  // Validation errors
   225→  if (
   226→    message.includes('required') ||
   227→    message.includes('invalid') ||
   228→    message.includes('validation')
   229→  ) {
   230→    return new ValidationError(err.message, { context, cause: err });
   231→  }
   232→
   233→  // Default to generic AppError
   234→  return new AppError(err.message, { context, cause: err });
   235→}
   236→

import { debugConfig } from './debug/debugConfig';
import { toJson } from '@/shared/lib/supabaseTypeHelpers';

// Lightweight logging helper that can be enabled/disabled via Vite env
// Usage:
//   import { log, time, timeEnd } from '@/shared/lib/logger';
//   log('MyTag', 'Some message', optionalData);
//   time('MyTag', 'expensive-operation');
//   ...do work...
//   timeEnd('MyTag', 'expensive-operation');
//
// Logs are only printed when `VITE_DEBUG_LOGS` is set to `true`.
// This avoids polluting the console in production while still allowing
// rich diagnostics for performance investigations.
//
// Log persistence (to system_logs table):
//   Set `VITE_PERSIST_LOGS=true` to buffer and send logs to system_logs.
//   When enabled, ALL console.log/warn/error calls are captured automatically.
//   Logs are batched and flushed every 10s or when buffer hits 50 entries.
//   Query with: SELECT * FROM system_logs WHERE source_type = 'browser'
//   Or use: debug.py logs --latest
//
// All logs share the same shape so they can be filtered easily.
// Tag format guideline (keep short & consistent):
//   [Area][Specific] e.g. [TaskPoller], [Render:GenerationsPane]

// ===== CONFIGURATION =====

const FLUSH_INTERVAL_MS = 10000; // Flush every 10 seconds
const FLUSH_BUFFER_SIZE = 100;   // Flush when buffer hits this size

function generateSessionId(): string {
  const timestamp = Date.now();
  const runtimeCrypto = globalThis.crypto;

  if (runtimeCrypto?.randomUUID) {
    return `browser-${timestamp}-${runtimeCrypto.randomUUID().slice(0, 8)}`;
  }

  if (runtimeCrypto?.getRandomValues) {
    const randomBytes = new Uint8Array(4);
    runtimeCrypto.getRandomValues(randomBytes);
    const randomHex = Array.from(randomBytes, (byte) => byte.toString(16).padStart(2, '0')).join('');
    return `browser-${timestamp}-${randomHex}`;
  }

  return `browser-${timestamp}-no-crypto`;
}

const SESSION_ID = generateSessionId();

1→/**
     2→ * Task ID resolution helpers
     3→ *
     4→ * Centralizes the logic for extracting task IDs from variant params,
     5→ * handling legacy field names consistently.
     6→ */
     7→
     8→const UUID_REGEX = /^[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}$/i;
     9→const CANONICAL_SOURCE_TASK_ID_PATHS = [
    10→  ['source_task_id'],
    11→  ['orchestration_contract', 'orchestrator_task_id'],
    12→];
    13→const LEGACY_SOURCE_TASK_ID_PATHS = [
    14→  ['orchestrator_task_id'],
    15→  ['task_id'],
    16→] as const;
    17→
    18→function readStringPath(
    19→  value: unknown,
    20→  path: readonly string[],
    21→): string | null {
    22→  let current: unknown = value;
    23→  for (const segment of path) {
    24→    if (!current || typeof current !== 'object' || Array.isArray(current)) {
    25→      return null;
    26→    }
    27→    current = (current as Record<string, unknown>)[segment];
    28→  }
    29→  return typeof current === 'string' && current.length > 0 ? current : null;
    30→}
    31→
    32→function resolveTaskIdFromPaths(
    33→  value: unknown,
    34→  paths: readonly (readonly string[])[],
    35→): string | null {
    36→  return paths
    37→    .map((path) => readStringPath(value, path))
    38→    .find((candidate): candidate is string => Boolean(candidate)) ?? null;
    39→}
    40→
    41→function asValidUuid(value: string | null): string | null {
    42→  if (!value) {
    43→    return null;
    44→  }
    45→  return UUID_REGEX.test(value) ? value : null;
    46→}
    47→
    48→/**
    49→ * Extract the source task ID from variant params.
    50→ *
    51→ * Variants can have their source task ID stored under different field names
    52→ * due to historical evolution of the param structure:
    53→ * - `source_task_id` - Current standard (preferred)
    54→ * - `orchestration_contract.orchestrator_task_id` - Canonical orchestrator contract
    55→ *
    56→ * @param params - Variant params object (typically from variant.params)
    57→ * @returns Valid UUID task ID, or null if not found/invalid
    58→ */
    59→export function getSourceTaskId(
    60→  params: Record<string, unknown> | null | undefined
    61→): string | null {
    62→  return asValidUuid(resolveTaskIdFromPaths(params, CANONICAL_SOURCE_TASK_ID_PATHS));

    69→export function getSourceTaskIdLegacyCompatible(

    34→  const mainQuery = useQuery<GenerationRow[], Error>({

    40→    // realtimeBacked provides staleTime: 30_000 — don't override to 0.
    41→    // staleTime: 0 makes the query perpetually stale, which combined with React Query's
    42→    // observer.setOptions() running every render causes a fetch→render→fetch loop.
    43→    // refetchOnMount: 'always' ensures fresh data when opening a shot without the loop.
    44→    refetchOnMount: 'always',
    45→    retry: STANDARD_RETRY,
    46→    // NOTE: Removed placeholderData: (previousData) => previousData
    47→    // This was causing cross-shot data leakage - when navigating to a new shot,
    48→    // the previous shot's images would briefly appear as "placeholder" data
    49→    queryFn: async ({ signal }) => {
    50→      // Query shot_generations with embedded generations data + primary variant

    54→      // to get the correct display URL (primary variant may differ from generation.location)
    55→      const response = await supabase().from('shot_generations')

    57→          id,
    58→          generation_id,
    59→          timeline_frame,
    60→          metadata,
    61→          generation:generations!shot_generations_generation_id_generations_id_fk (

    63→            location,
    64→            thumbnail_url,
    65→            type,
    66→            created_at,
    67→            starred,
    68→            name,
    69→            based_on,
    70→            params,
    71→            primary_variant_id,
    72→            primary_variant:generation_variants!generations_primary_variant_id_fkey (
    73→              location,
    74→              thumbnail_url
    75→            )
    76→          )
    77→        `)
    78→        .eq('shot_id', stableShotId!)
    79→        .order('timeline_frame', { ascending: true, nullsFirst: false })
    80→        .abortSignal(signal);

    91→          logData: { shotId: stableShotId },

    96→      return (response.data || [])
    97→        .map(mapShotGenerationToRow)
    98→        .filter(Boolean) as GenerationRow[];
    99→    },
   100→    retryDelay: STANDARD_RETRY_DELAY,

   102→
   103→  return mainQuery as UseQueryResult<GenerationRow[]>;

   106→/** Positioned, non-video images with valid location, sorted by timeline_frame. */
   107→export const useTimelineImages = (
   108→  shotId: string | null
   109→): UseQueryResult<GenerationRow[]> => {
   110→  const baseQuery = useAllShotGenerations(shotId);
   111→
   112→  const filtered = React.useMemo(() => {
   113→    if (!baseQuery.data) return undefined;
   114→
   115→    return baseQuery.data
   116→      .filter(g => {
   117→        const location = g.imageUrl || g.location;
   118→        const hasValidLocation = location && location !== '/placeholder.svg';
   119→        return g.timeline_frame != null &&
   120→               g.timeline_frame >= 0 &&
   121→               !g.type?.includes('video') &&
   122→               hasValidLocation;
   123→      })
   124→      .sort((a, b) => (a.timeline_frame ?? 0) - (b.timeline_frame ?? 0));
   125→  }, [baseQuery.data]);
   126→
   127→  return { ...baseQuery, data: filtered } as UseQueryResult<GenerationRow[]>;
   128→};
   129→
   130→/** Non-video images with no timeline_frame. */
   131→export const useUnpositionedImages = (
   132→  shotId: string | null
   133→): UseQueryResult<GenerationRow[]> => {

   146→  }, [baseQuery.data]);

    13→const NON_PRELOADABLE_URL_MARKERS = ['_joined_frame.jpg'] as const;
    14→
    15→/**
    16→ * Get the canonical generation ID from a media item.
    17→ * Handles both direct generations (id) and variants (generation_id).
    18→ * Also checks metadata.generation_id for compatibility with various data shapes.
    19→ *
    20→ * Priority: generation_id > metadata.generation_id > id
    21→ *
    22→ * @example
    23→ * // Instead of: (media as unknown).generation_id || media.id
    24→ * const genId = getGenerationId(media);
    25→ */
    26→export function getGenerationId(
    27→  media: MaybeHasGenerationId | null | undefined
    28→): string | null {
    29→  if (!media) return null;
    30→  const metadataGenerationId = typeof media.metadata?.generation_id === 'string'
    31→    ? media.metadata.generation_id
    32→    : null;
    33→  return media.generation_id || metadataGenerationId || media.id || null;
    34→}
    35→
    36→/**

    39→export function isPreloadableMediaUrl(url: string | null | undefined): boolean {
    40→  if (!url) {

    42→  }
    43→
    44→  return !NON_PRELOADABLE_URL_MARKERS.some((marker) => url.includes(marker));

1→/**
     2→ * Canonical eligibility contract for "timeline-positioned images":
     3→ * - positioned frame (timeline_frame >= 0)
     4→ * - not a video media item
     5→ */
     6→
     7→const VIDEO_EXTENSIONS = ['.mp4', '.webm', '.mov'] as const;
     8→const VIDEO_TYPES = new Set(['video', 'video_travel_output']);
     9→
    10→export interface TimelineEligibilityInput {
    11→  timeline_frame?: number | null;
    12→  type?: string | null;
    13→  location?: string | null;
    14→  imageUrl?: string | null;
    15→  url?: string | null;
    16→  generation?: {
    17→    type?: string | null;
    18→    location?: string | null;
    19→  } | null;
    20→}
    21→
    22→export function hasTimelineVideoExtension(url: string | null | undefined): boolean {
    23→  if (!url) return false;
    24→  const lower = url.toLowerCase();
    25→  return VIDEO_EXTENSIONS.some((ext) => lower.endsWith(ext));
    26→}
    27→
    28→export function isTimelineVideoType(type: string | null | undefined): boolean {
    29→  if (!type) return false;
    30→  return VIDEO_TYPES.has(type);
    31→}
    32→
    33→export function isTimelineVideoLike(input: Pick<TimelineEligibilityInput, 'type' | 'location' | 'imageUrl' | 'url' | 'generation'>): boolean {
    34→  if (isTimelineVideoType(input.type)) return true;
    35→  if (hasTimelineVideoExtension(input.location)) return true;
    36→  if (hasTimelineVideoExtension(input.imageUrl)) return true;
    37→  if (hasTimelineVideoExtension(input.url)) return true;
    38→  if (isTimelineVideoType(input.generation?.type)) return true;
    39→  if (hasTimelineVideoExtension(input.generation?.location)) return true;
    40→  return false;
    41→}
    42→
    43→export function hasPositionedTimelineFrame(timelineFrame: number | null | undefined): boolean {
    44→  return timelineFrame != null && timelineFrame >= 0;
    45→}
    46→
    47→export function isTimelineEligiblePositionedImage(input: TimelineEligibilityInput): boolean {
    48→  if (!hasPositionedTimelineFrame(input.timeline_frame)) {
    49→    return false;
    50→  }
    51→  return !isTimelineVideoLike(input);
    52→}
    53→
    54→export function filterTimelineEligiblePositionedImages<T extends TimelineEligibilityInput>(
    55→  rows: T[],
    56→): T[] {
    57→  return rows.filter((row) => isTimelineEligiblePositionedImage(row));
    58→}

     4→ * SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for transforming generation data from database to UI format.

/** @publicContract Supabase browser runtime entrypoint. */

import {
  type SupabaseClientAccessResult,
  getSupabaseRuntimeClientResult,
  initializeSupabaseClientRuntime,
  normalizeSupabaseError,
} from '@/integrations/supabase/runtime/supabaseRuntime';

export type { SupabaseClientAccessResult };

export interface SupabaseClientRegistry {
  getClientResult: () => SupabaseClientAccessResult;
}

/** Runtime bootstrap entrypoint for app startup. */
export function initializeSupabase() {
  return initializeSupabaseClientRuntime();
}

export function initializeSupabaseResult(): SupabaseClientAccessResult {
  try {
    const client = initializeSupabase();
    return { ok: true, client };
  } catch (error) {
    return { ok: false, error: normalizeSupabaseError(error) };
  }
}

/** Runtime accessor that never throws; callers can branch on initialization state. */
export function getSupabaseClientResult(): SupabaseClientAccessResult {
  const result = getSupabaseRuntimeClientResult();
  return result.ok ? result : { ok: false, error: normalizeSupabaseError(result.error) };
}

export const supabaseClientRegistry: SupabaseClientRegistry = {
  getClientResult: getSupabaseClientResult,
};

/** Runtime accessor for initialized app runtime. Throws if bootstrap has not run. */
export function getSupabaseClient() {
  const result = supabaseClientRegistry.getClientResult();
  if (!result.ok) {
    throw result.error;
  }
  return result.client;
}

function filterReferenceSettingsByMode(
  referenceMode: 'style' | 'subject' | 'style-character' | 'scene' | 'custom' | undefined,
  settings: {
    style_reference_strength?: number;
    subject_strength?: number;
    subject_description?: string;
    in_this_scene?: boolean;
    in_this_scene_strength?: number;
  }
): Partial<typeof settings> {
  // If no mode specified or custom mode, pass all settings as-is
  if (!referenceMode || referenceMode === 'custom') {
    return settings;
  }

  const filtered: Partial<typeof settings> = {};
  
  switch (referenceMode) {
    case 'style':
      // Style mode: only pass style strength, exclude subject and scene
      if (settings.style_reference_strength !== undefined) {
        filtered.style_reference_strength = settings.style_reference_strength;
      }
      break;

    case 'subject':
      // Subject mode: style at 1.1, subject at 0.5, plus description
      filtered.style_reference_strength = 1.1;
      filtered.subject_strength = 0.5;
      if (settings.subject_description !== undefined && settings.subject_description.trim()) {
        filtered.subject_description = settings.subject_description;
      }
      break;

    case 'style-character':
      // Style + Subject mode: pass both style and subject, exclude scene
      if (settings.style_reference_strength !== undefined) {
        filtered.style_reference_strength = settings.style_reference_strength;
      }
      if (settings.subject_strength !== undefined) {
        filtered.subject_strength = settings.subject_strength;
      }
      if (settings.subject_description !== undefined && settings.subject_description.trim()) {
        filtered.subject_description = settings.subject_description;
      }
      break;

    case 'scene':
      // Scene mode: style at 1.1, scene strength at 0.5
      filtered.style_reference_strength = 1.1;
      filtered.in_this_scene = true;
      filtered.in_this_scene_strength = 0.5;
      break;
  }
  
  return filtered;
}

  custom_aspect_ratio?: string;
  model_name?: string;
  subject_reference_image?: string; // Can differ from style_reference_image
  steps?: number;
}
